commit.message:
Integrate qualified HIA .hepta source tree without changing tested bytes

Preserve main5831, published9a12 and localbbc development histories.
The complete tree is byte/mode-identical to bbc5551:178.hepta,528source
checks, own cold11/5049,57native stages and4657 full tests with original
limits and independent replays. No later standalone storage development
is included. Python/SQLite/runtime duties remain transitional; this is
not a claim of whole native product closure or legacy retirement.

Merge native signatures and task helpers into HIA closure

Combine exact main d6847ac with native worker-request admission and immutable release installation. Preserve the public fixture admissions while retaining private construction optimization and all existing native gates.

Add a joint native type/signature/origin and task-helper witness that requires one matching current-source cold receipt and prohibits retained owners. Extend CI and the complete-source v5 qualification runner with all merged owner groups.

Regenerate all 42 HIA source generators byte-for-byte, refresh the language inventory and pin 583 source files in the distinct v63 support contract. Historical v62 passes remain tied to their sources; v63 cold and full retained qualification are pending. Whole-native delivery and production retirement remain open.

Integrate current main with native request and release closure

Join exact main f50b375 and PR888 93d66bcc without overwriting either development line. Regenerate complete source identity and inventory for the combined candidate. Existing qualification remains attached to its original source; this checkpoint is not whole-native acceptance.

+name: HIA candidate bindings
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: ['codex/hia-three-loop-*']
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - 'hepta/**'
+      - 'tools/hia_candidate_preflight.py'
+      - 'tools/generate_hia_agent_native_contract.py'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_checker_identity*.py'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_worker_native_helpers.py'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_worker_request*.py'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_original_select_extension.py'
+      - 'tools/qualify_hia_original_select_extension.py'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_candidate*.py'
+      - '.github/workflows/hia-candidate-bindings.yml'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+jobs:
+  bindings:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.14'
+      - name: Install the existing qualified native prerequisites
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key
+          fingerprint=$(gpg --show-keys --with-colons "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" | awk -F: '$1 == "fpr" { print $10; exit }')
+          test "$fingerprint" = 6084F3CF814B57C1CF12EFD515CF4D18AF4F7421
+          sudo install -m 0644 "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" /usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc
+          printf '%s\n' 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc] https://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-20 main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/hia-llvm20.list
+          sudo apt-get update
+          sudo apt-get install -y binutils gcc clang-20 libclang-rt-20-dev
+          printf 'CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\nHEPTA_CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\n' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          python -m pip install setuptools==78.1.1 wheel==0.46.3 z3-solver==4.15.4.0 jsonschema==4.26.0
+      - name: Independently regenerate the shared tool catalog without changing source
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings"
+          python -B - <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings/catalog.log"
+          import os, pathlib, shutil, subprocess, sys
+          root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
+          temp = pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "hia-catalog-regeneration"
+          (temp / "tools").mkdir(parents=True)
+          (temp / "docs").mkdir()
+          for name in ("tools/generate_hia_agent_native_contract.py", "docs/HIA_AGENT_NATIVE_RUNTIME_CONTRACT.md"):
+              shutil.copyfile(root / name, temp / name)
+          subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(temp / "tools/generate_hia_agent_native_contract.py")], check=True)
+          assert (temp / "docs/HIA_AGENT_NATIVE_TOOL_CATALOG.json").read_bytes() == (root / "docs/HIA_AGENT_NATIVE_TOOL_CATALOG.json").read_bytes()
+          shutil.copyfile(temp / "docs/HIA_AGENT_NATIVE_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_CHECK.json",
+                          pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "hia-candidate-bindings" / "catalog-schema-check.json")
+          PY
+      - name: Run exact-source custody proof and actual native worker controls
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings"
+          git rev-parse HEAD > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings/source.sha"
+          git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings/source.tree"
+          python -B tools/generate_hia_selfhost_contract.py --check
+          python -B - <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-candidate-bindings/tests.log"
+          import json, os, pathlib, subprocess, time, unittest
+          names = (
+              "tests.test_hia_candidate_preflight",
+              "tests.test_hia_candidate_evidence",
+              "tests.test_hia_checker_identity",
+              "tests.test_hia_checker_identity_agent",
+              "tests.test_hia_scalar_proof_contract",
+              "tests.test_hia_safe_core_artifact",
+              "tests.test_hia_agent_native_proof_contract",
+              "tests.test_hia_agent_native_machine_validation",
+              "tests.test_hia_worker_native_helpers",
+              "tests.test_hia_worker_request_native",
+              "tests.test_hia_worker_request_review",
+              "tests.test_hia_original_select_extension",
+          )
+          started = time.monotonic()
+          result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromNames(names))
+          passed = result.wasSuccessful() and not result.skipped and not result.expectedFailures
+          summary = {
+              "schema": "hepta.hia.candidate-bindings-tests.v1",
+              "source_sha": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip(),
+              "source_tree": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], text=True).strip(),
+              "tests": result.testsRun, "failures": len(result.failures), "errors": len(result.errors),
+              "skips": len(result.skipped), "expected_failures": len(result.expectedFailures),
+              "unexpected_successes": len(result.unexpectedSuccesses),
+              "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started, "passed": passed,
+              "full_cold_replay_qualified": False, "production_connector_deployed": False,
+              "whole_native_worker_qualified": False,
+          }
+          path = pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "hia-candidate-bindings" / "summary.json"
+          path.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+          print(json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True))
+          raise SystemExit(0 if passed else 1)
+          PY
+          git diff --exit-code
+      - name: Retain original output on both failure and success
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: hia-candidate-bindings-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 14
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hia-candidate-bindings/

+name: HIA original compiler extension
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: ['codex/hia-three-loop-*']

+    paths:
+      - 'hepta/**'
+      - 'tools/**'
+      - 'tests/test_hia_original_select_extension.py'
+      - 'tests/fixtures/hia_original_select_v1/**'
+      - 'docs/HIA_SELFHOST_CORE_SUPPORT.json'
+      - '.github/workflows/hia-compiler-extension.yml'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+jobs:
+  original-select:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    env:
+      EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Start the original evidence record
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension"
+          printf '%s\n' "$EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/expected-source.sha"
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+      - name: Bind the exact source candidate
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA"
+          git rev-parse HEAD > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source.sha"
+          git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source.tree"
+          git status --porcelain=v1 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source-status-before.txt"
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.14'
+      - name: Install the existing qualified native prerequisites
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key
+          fingerprint=$(gpg --show-keys --with-colons "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" | awk -F: '$1 == "fpr" { print $10; exit }')
+          test "$fingerprint" = 6084F3CF814B57C1CF12EFD515CF4D18AF4F7421
+          printf '%s\n' "$fingerprint" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/llvm-key-fingerprint.txt"
+          sudo install -m 0644 "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-llvm.asc" /usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc
+          printf '%s\n' 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/hia-llvm.asc] https://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-20 main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/hia-llvm20.list
+          sudo apt-get update 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/apt-update.log"
+          sudo apt-get install -y binutils gcc clang-20 libclang-rt-20-dev 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/apt-install.log"
+          printf 'CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\nHEPTA_CLANG=/usr/bin/clang-20\n' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+          python -m pip install setuptools==78.1.1 wheel==0.46.3 z3-solver==4.15.4.0 jsonschema==4.26.0 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/pip-install.log"
+          python --version > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/python-version.txt"
+          clang-20 --version > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/clang-version.txt"
+          ld --version > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/linker-version.txt"
+      - name: Check the finite-domain negative controls
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python -B tools/generate_hia_selfhost_contract.py --check 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source-contract.log"
+          python -B - <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/unit-tests.log"
+          import json, os, pathlib, unittest
+          suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromName("tests.test_hia_original_select_extension")
+          result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
+          passed = result.wasSuccessful() and result.testsRun == 6 and not result.skipped and not result.expectedFailures
+          summary = {"tests": result.testsRun, "failures": len(result.failures), "errors": len(result.errors),
+                     "skips": len(result.skipped), "expected_failures": len(result.expectedFailures),
+                     "passed": passed, "native_qualification_is_separate": True}
+          (pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "hia-compiler-extension/unit-tests.json").write_text(
+              json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+          raise SystemExit(0 if passed else 1)
+          PY
+      - name: Recover the exact historical maintenance subjects
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          curl --fail --location --retry 3 --max-time 120 \
+            --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/original-raw-evidence.zip" \
+            https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Hepta/6502316907b10fba822b3518d0ba2cc7417afa61/review-evidence/hia-agent-original-select-delta-20261108-5e6c/raw-evidence.zip \
+            2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/archive-download.log"
+          python -B - <<'PY' 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/archive-check.log"
+          import hashlib, json, os, pathlib
+          path = pathlib.Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]) / "hia-compiler-extension/original-raw-evidence.zip"
+          raw = path.read_bytes()
+          actual = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+          assert len(raw) == 4233093
+          assert actual == "0b18f5665657601141ada5fe67990ee192d91665eb5463f806b495d6240a2d3a"
+          print(json.dumps({"archive_sha256": actual, "archive_bytes": len(raw)}, sort_keys=True))
+          PY
+      - name: Run both original compilers and replay the scoped fragment obligations
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python -B tools/qualify_hia_original_select_extension.py \
+            --historical-archive "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/original-raw-evidence.zip" \
+            --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/qualification" \
+            2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/qualification.log"
+          git diff --exit-code 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source-diff-after.log"
+          git status --porcelain=v1 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/hia-compiler-extension/source-status-after.txt"
+      - name: Retain all original outputs on failure and success
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: hia-compiler-extension-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 14
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hia-compiler-extension/

+# HIA artifact namespace owner
+
+## Development scope
+
+This document specifies the next owner under implementation. It is not a
+qualification report, runtime default change, or full-stack closure claim.
+The source baseline is the exact tree
+`ac479ebeceef01fccae7260f2954d5766f44640e` recovered from the saved request-journal
+archive. Recovery commit `829e1d6cd626d8479dcce160a59523381a12e9f9` has new
+history; it does not recreate original commit `56cf394`.
+
+The indivisible boundary is `AgentStore.put`, `json`, `get`, `get_json`,
+`resolve_uri`, `profile` and `check_profile`. A separate native byte publisher
+already performs content hashing, bounded reads, immutable no-replace
+publication, file fsync and directory fsync. The remaining namespace decisions
+must move together: content/metadata binding, reference issuance, exact row and
+kind authority, URI resolution, and profile-to-artifact correspondence.
+
+The existing tables remain authoritative:
+
+```text
+main.artifacts(id, sha256, uri, kind, metadata, content_key)
+main.profiles(id, sha256, artifact)
+```
+
+There is no replacement database, namespace reset, row migration, content
+overwrite, reference garbage collection, or automatic retry of an unknown
+operation. Existing caller-owned transactions retain their atomic boundary.
+
+## Native state and effect interface
+
+One retained HIA state belongs to each selected `AgentStore`. It carries a
+store nonce, monotonic sequence, current operation identity, captured immutable
+input bytes, exact SQL connection/scope identity, pending effect token and
+outcome. It is not reconstructed from Python boolean flags on each call.
+
+Every foreign effect has three native transitions:
+
+1. Stage the exact effect and its immutable inputs.
+2. Consume its launch claim before SQL or publisher execution.
+3. Accept one matching outcome for that claim and operation/scope identity.
+
+Pending or unknown effects block ordinary reentry. A Python return-value or
+diagnostic-store interruption cannot restore launch authority. Observation is
+a separate read-only native entry; it cannot clear a claim or authorize replay.
+State corruption, sequence exhaustion, wrong owner/connection/epoch and stale
+outcome tokens refuse. Checksums are corruption checks, not protection against
+malicious code with same-process access to native memory.
+
+The native policy composes the exact canonical content-key bytes from retained
+kind, metadata and content hash. The existing canonical JSON codec remains a
+foreign value bridge, and metadata is frozen once before effects. Content and
+binding hashes come from the admitted HIA publisher. HIA forms UUID4 reference
+bytes from supplied entropy. A selected namespace requires that native byte
+dependency; it has no hosted hash/read/write fallback.
+
+## Exact row and file custody
+
+An existing content-key row must match the exact content hash, kind and frozen
+metadata before it can be reused. A publication receipt does not issue a
+database reference. `INSERT OR IGNORE` permits a concurrent dedup winner only
+after exact row readback; an unrelated ID/URI collision cannot supply a ref.
+References are checked against their original namespace row before file reads.
+URI resolution binds the observed URI row and its subsequent identity lookup.
+
+Profile registration and verification include the profile row, the referenced
+artifact row, its `profile` kind and actual file bytes. Success at one lookup
+cannot replace the remaining observations. Every SQL statement is qualified
+with `main`; TEMP namespaces cannot become authority. Each observation has its
+own native outcome token.
+
+Known input/authority refusals preserve ordinary rejection semantics.
+Unconfirmed publication, SQL execution or acknowledgement preserves the native
+pending operation and raises a nonterminal error. That error must bypass the
+request-journal terminal rejection formatter. Files may remain after a failed
+or interrupted database step; their presence alone never proves completion of
+the original request.
+
+## Transaction scopes
+
+Three connection scopes are distinct:
+
+| Scope | Required custody |
+| --- | --- |
+| Original official connection in autocommit mode | Original main/WAL identity, creator PID, actual connection and no enclosing transaction |
+| Existing `AgentStore.transaction()` | Native-issued scope nonce/epoch bound to the original official connection, plus exact BEGIN/end claims |
+| Explicit request `_EffectConnection` | Its actual native request nonce, connection identity, transaction epoch and pending callback token, rechecked before effects |
+
+The namespace owner never commits an explicit request capability. It returns
+row authority within that supplied transaction; the request owner still commits
+slot changes and exact response together. A revoked request capability cannot
+be replaced with the autocommit connection to finish a pending operation.
+
+The four original service `store.transaction()` callers are the reference
+request admission/atomic path and lease acquire/release; the retained reference
+budget also uses that original transaction helper. Their original connection and
+transaction boundary remain. Native scope state must preclaim BEGIN, COMMIT
+and ROLLBACK and retain unknown outcomes. Namespace-operation and enclosing
+scope pending slots are distinct: one legitimate SQL rollback may follow an
+unknown namespace operation without overwriting that operation's uncertainty.
+The original request intent remains the durable operation journal.
+
+When namespace and request owners are both selected, their adapters share the
+original `AgentStore.lock`. Both official and private transaction entry take
+that lock before SQLite's write lock. This prevents a private request callback
+waiting for the namespace lock while a legacy transaction holds that lock and
+waits for the private SQLite writer. The database handles and HIA states remain
+distinct. Unselected request behavior retains its original separate lock.
+
+## Explicit compatibility limits and strengthenings
+
+The supported public input scope uses exact byte payloads, UTF-8 string kinds
+and profile identifiers, canonical issued artifact references, and the original
+bounded JSON value bridge. Payloads retain the inclusive 64 MiB quota; canonical
+JSON and each text field are bounded by 8 MiB. A supported legacy profile row
+contains the exact canonical 176-byte artifact reference emitted by the
+original `wire(ref)`. Arbitrarily edited SQLite rows, nonstring kinds and
+unbounded diagnostic identifiers are not claimed as an arbitrary-object API
+equivalence result.
+
+Metadata is serialized once. Both newly issued and existing rows bind that
+exact byte string. Read operations also recompute the content-key binding from
+the observed content hash, kind and metadata, using the native byte owner's
+hash operation. Profile lookup verifies that its artifact hash equals the
+profile hash. These are explicit integrity strengthenings of the reference
+implementation's weaker row checks.
+
+The fixed publisher bridge now distinguishes an actual returned process refusal
+from unavailable execution or a lost/invalid receipt. It retains the original
+`PublicationRejected` superclass and message. HIA may accept an exact confirmed
+read-only/hash refusal; no mutating publication refusal or unconfirmed handoff
+grants a retry. Byte-owner admission can cancel only a first staged namespace
+operation whose native launch count is still zero. This cancellation cannot
+clear any operation that has started an effect.
+
+The native scope cleanup guard consumes its epoch even when the original
+connection is observed outside a transaction. A later foreign transaction
+cannot acquire that old cleanup authority. A lost COMMIT/ROLLBACK receipt keeps
+the scope uncertain even when an independent observation finds no transaction.
+The original reference method bodies remain separately named and selected only
+when the namespace owner is absent.
+
+## Required qualification before integration
+
+The completed owner needs independent VM and actual-machine policy controls,
+original/native API comparisons, exact metadata binding and UUID formatting,
+content dedup races, main/TEMP isolation, profile/row/file corruption controls,
+native publisher receipt loss, actual SQL acknowledgement loss, reentry and
+revoked-scope controls, process-crash/restart observations, and installed-wheel
+execution with original namespace policy and authoring imports forbidden.
+
+Joint controls must run the actual request and execution-budget owners, actual
+adopt/rollback and leases, and the existing byte publisher. Development compiler
+reuse remains labelled development. Integrated qualification requires one
+matching current-source cold report for all selected dependencies. No passing
+result or completed implementation is asserted by this design checkpoint.

+It is a development image, not a current-source cold qualification.
+The historical development report records 24 passing tests: 17 call owner

+differential cases, 1457 malformed packet cases, and a complete 4,198,912
+element call argument result. Those are observations about the frozen source
+and historical harnesses. The replacement suite requires its own execution.
+
+## Owned behavior
+
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/call_primitive.hiaasm` owns ordinary nominal calls and
+the erasure of primitive instructions in an admitted nominal function. Its
+decisions include:
+
+- Call attribute inventory, callee identifier admission, and signature lookup.
+- Exact argument and return type correspondence, including distinct nominal
+  identities with equal primitive layouts.
+- Output reparse ordering, ordered linear consumption, and generated-name
+  allocation.
+- Complete returned Core instructions, consumed-value flags, and output
+  bindings, including the prefix produced before a semantic refusal.
+- Primitive nominal-type guards and the original consuming-operation set:
+  `owner.move`, `owner.drop`, `loan.end`, `chain.try_push`, and `chain.pop`.
+
+The installed bridge copies already held object identities into descriptor
+IDs. It forwards two explicit requests to the existing signature and type
+owners, and decodes the HIA-produced complete result. It does not implement a
+second call lookup, type comparison, ownership policy, or instruction plan.
+
+The primitive Core verifier still validates the generated instruction and
+whole program. A native erasure result is not execution authority. In
+particular, an unfamiliar primitive opcode or its raw attributes can survive
+this erasure stage and be refused by the ordinary later Core check, preserving
+the previous error order.
+
+## Continuation protocol and publication order
+
+The private input is a typed object array containing phase, generated-name
+counter, operation, attributes, type descriptors, deduplicated held values,
+argument references, declared outputs, signature inventory, and reparsed
+outputs. Repeated argument aliases refer to the same held value descriptor.
+Nominal type identities are transported by exact object identity rather than
+display names, hashes, or Python semantic equality.
+
+For a valid call the sequence is:
+
+1. Phase 0 checks the attributes and callee name, then requests the signature
+   inventory. Invalid attributes and names refuse before that callback.
+2. Phase 1 looks up the callee and compares argument types, then requests output
+   reparse. An absent callee or argument mismatch refuses before output reparse.
+3. Phase 2 compares the reparsed outputs, consumes owned arguments in order,
+   allocates generated names, and returns the complete Core call and bindings.
+
+Primitive erasure uses phase 0 and requests neither callback.
+The driver performs at most three native steps per `lower()` invocation.
+This is an in-process continuation protocol; it is not a persistent request
+journal or a promise of replay resistance for externally retained private
+packets. A callback exception propagates from that invocation.
+
+The result header has eight little-endian u64 fields: `HIACPR01` magic,
+semantic error, final counter, request, payload size, and three zero reserved
+words. The payload contains exactly `ops`, `consumed`, `values`, and `query`.
+The adapter checks extents, exact scalar types, phase/request correlation,
+counter bounds, graph structure, and immutable input bytes before returning a
+result. The elaborator publishes the returned counter, operations, consumed
+flags, and completed bindings before raising its semantic error. This retains
+the original partial-state order.
+
+For example, a call that consumes an owner and then exhausts its generated-name
+budget may return the consumed flag and completed earlier bindings while
+emitting no call instruction. Replacing that result with an empty generic
+failure would lose observable state and is not permitted.
+
+## Storage and lossless graphs
+
+| Region or bound | Limit |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Private encoded input | 256 MiB |
+| Native output | 64 MiB |
+| Native workspace | 32 MiB |
+| Generated-name counter | 8192 |
+| Held value and argument inventories | 262144 each |
+| Type descriptor inventory | 524288 |
+| Signature inventory | 1024 |
+| Primitive width of one nominal type | 512 |
+| Declared output primitive slots | 32768 |
+
+These private transport limits do not relax the public source or Core limits.
+The checked-in generator also remains within the existing native compiler
+function, block, instruction, and block-parameter budgets.
+
+The generic graph codec can reference original encoded nodes and concatenate
+original arrays. Thus a repeated 512-slot argument can be represented without
+repeating all of its strings in the native output frame. Decoding still creates
+the complete logical argument list; it does not truncate, summarize, hash, or
+replace that list with a promise. The source document and its later public
+value-slot/Core rejection remain unchanged.
+
+## Selection, installation, and cold admission
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_CALL_PRIMITIVE_MANIFEST` selects the installed native owner. The
+manifest binds the HIA source, executable image, schema, and compiler identity.
+Missing, malformed, stale, or mismatched selected artifacts refuse. They do not
+authorize execution of `_reference_call_primitive`. An unselected process
+retains the existing reference route until a later repository-wide cutover.
+
+Installed resources are package-owned. The wheel controls run with an empty
+`PATH`, disable the hosted call branch, and prevent importing authoring tools.
+They compare the complete canonical Core bytes, then remove or change the
+installed HIA resource and require a refusal.
+
+The replacement fixture has separate development and cold paths:
+
+- `HEPTA_HIA_CALL_PRIMITIVE_DEVELOPMENT_MANIFEST` uses a supplied, source-bound
+  development artifact. It confers no cold qualification.
+- `HEPTA_HIA_CALL_PRIMITIVE_COLD_REPORT` uses the normal standalone builder and

+

+
+## Replacement controls

+Each original foreign command 1–41, the selfhost call 42, handler cleanup 43
+and pending-argument read 44 require a native preclaim. A claim binds the live session nonce, command and
+monotone sequence. HIA marks it consumed before the adapter launches the first
+callback. A repeated claim, cross-session claim, malformed outcome, lost native
+ACK or interrupted effect fences the session. No handler, retry or fallback
+obtains a second permission for an uncertain effect.

+still owns actual Python reference transfers, function calls, exception frames

+preserve the emitted output of two registered old source files and correctly
+handle a registered finite set of new select programs and runtime inputs.
+Its schema is `hepta.hia.compiler-extension.finite-domain.v1`.

+# Constructor candidate: bounds and outer-owner interface
+
+This is an implementation argument for the isolated constructor candidate. It
+does not establish current-source cold qualification, activate a default path,
+or justify removing the retained implementation. The recovered implementation
+base is `f50b37543d1a379353267ce0ab7111242806b8b4` plus the frozen full-function
+overlay. The older design document records the pre-restart design context;
+the current source identities are in the development stage manifests.
+
+## Original input bounds
+
+The public verifier admits a detached exact JSON tree before nominal
+elaboration. Let `N <= 262144` be its value-node count and `B <= 8388608` its
+canonical JSON byte count. Dictionary keys are not additional value nodes,
+but there are at most `N - 1` dictionary edges/keys. The typed packet uses a
+16-byte header per value/key, 8 bytes per container count, and scalar payload
+bytes no larger than their canonical JSON spelling. Thus the complete
+`[document, legacy_bool]` packet is at most
+
+`40*N + B + 41 = 18874409 bytes`.
+
+This is below the unchanged 64 MiB generic input region. The packet wrapper
+adds one nesting level; the generic transport's 128-level/1048576-node framing
+ceiling is above the original public structural ceiling, including key nodes.
+It does not replace the public source bound. Exact unsupported Python objects
+are not another admission route.
+
+## Constructor arena charging
+
+The HIA constructor stores source references and issued type IDs. It never
+expands a type layout or Core body. The arena begins at `64 MiB + 65536` inside
+a 192 MiB workspace, leaving 134152192 bytes. Allocation is rounded to 8 bytes;
+the following charges include this rounding.
+
+For each successfully admitted formal parameter, the response ID costs 8
+bytes, its complete parameter-row IR and linked-list segments cost 192 bytes,
+and its name hash table costs less than 64 bytes per parameter. A zero-entry
+table costs 32 bytes and is charged to the function constant. Each formal has
+at least three source value nodes (the parameter object, name, and type).
+
+For every return reference, its request IR costs 160 bytes, the response ID
+costs 8 bytes, the retained ID vector costs 8 bytes, and its return-list IR
+costs 64 bytes: 240 bytes total. In v4, a null origin adds 16 bytes of checked
+slot metadata and 64 bytes of IR, for a total charge of 320 bytes per return.
+This includes the implicit null-origin case, which adds no annotation source
+nodes.
+
+A nonnull v4 origin adds at most 352 bytes: 16 checked-slot bytes, at most 144
+bytes for a length-prefixed 128-byte ASCII parameter name, and 192 bytes of
+origin pair/list IR. Together with its return, that is at most 592 bytes. A
+successful nonnull annotation requires at least three additional source value
+nodes (annotation object, parameter name, and field-path list). Its combined
+592-byte charge is therefore below 320 bytes per source node. Invalid origin
+responses are refused; an ordinary native origin error emits no origin payload
+and cannot exceed the successful allocation case.
+
+These return and parameter nodes are disjoint source occurrences. Repeated
+immutable strings and repeated type references still count separately in the
+public source budget. A typed request is issued once per source occurrence;
+response replay and phase changes refuse. No memory bound relies on input
+object deduplication or caching a previous admission.
+
+The remaining fixed IR, request envelopes, zero-parameter tables and registry
+rows fit conservatively in 4096 bytes per function. Every concrete task uses
+one resolution and one protocol request; 4096 bytes per declaration covers
+both and their response IDs. A further 65536 bytes covers the global function
+name table, initialization, final state envelope, and fixed list heads. With
+the unchanged `F <= 1024` functions and `D <= 128` definitions, a conservative
+total arena bound is
+
+`320*N + 4096*F + 4096*D + 65536 = 88670208 bytes`.
+
+This leaves 45481984 bytes below the actual arena capacity. The proof is about
+the HIA arena, not the Python interpreter's RSS. Source custody indexes,
+materialized objects and the separately bounded 128 MiB native type state are
+distinct allocations. The temporary constructor arena is released before the
+complete function session allocates its own arena. Final state and typed
+request streams use fixed 64 KiB chunks; no additional total-output quota is
+introduced.
+
+## State and continuation boundaries
+
+Initialization stages preserve absent attributes separately from empty maps:
+no owner fields; document/counters/profile; committed native type owner and
+returned-loan flag; and finally all five ordered inventories. A v4 origin row
+is committed before effects, while its function and signature are committed
+after effects. Every return resolves before the stored-loan gate. Unused task
+validation happens after all signatures and follows declaration order.
+
+The bridge publishes only native-issued complete state. Requests use a
+detached packet index; final source references use an exact, byte-bound index
+of the caller's already detached objects. This preserves document/function
+identity aliases while isolating service inputs. The complete source packet
+is read back before committing source references. Native type cache/work
+changes are never rolled back.
+
+Visible resume phases are 10, 30, 41, 50, 81, 82 and final 2000. Request kinds,
+request sequence, initialization stage, issued phase and profile must agree.
+A response is consumed once. Malformed native frames refuse at the bridge;
+malformed input/response buffers poison the HIA workspace itself. Both levels
+need actual boundary tests; a source-level argument alone is insufficient.
+
+## Future complete outer `lower` owner (design only)
+
+The retained outer method still controls source-function order, appends helper
+functions, checks Core function/block inventories only after all functions,
+sorts eligible primitive exports, and constructs the final program envelope.
+These semantics are not part of this constructor change.
+
+A future indivisible HIA outer owner should hold the source function cursor,
+the persistent native function session and helper append identities. It must
+request every complete function in source order before applying the existing
+final inventory check. Early per-function output-size refusal is incorrect:
+a complete function can exceed 8 MiB, and a later function error must still
+precede the final outer expansion refusal.
+
+The generic codec can retain complete native-issued function objects under
+opaque, single-session object identities. HIA would choose the final function
+and helper reference sequence and return the entire program IR. The host

+plan, counting blocks, choosing exports, or sorting names. Function/block
+counts must originate in the native function owner. Export classification
+must read its issued native type descriptors, and sorting must be HIA-owned.
+The public primitive verifier must still independently admit the completed
+Core. This proposed interface needs separate correlation, large-output,
+error-order and installed-package evidence before activation.

+# Complete HIA composite constructor candidate
+
+Status: new isolated implementation design. No constructor, default-path,
+cold, compiler, whole-language, or retained-owner removal claim is made here.
+The candidate is based on `1e8d554cb87e2a88adb5085b1e975812c23829b6` plus the
+frozen full-function overlay, recorded byte-for-byte in the development
+directory's `baseline.json`. The complete function terms deliverable remains
+frozen in its separate worktree.

+## Indivisible ownership
+
+HIA will own the whole original `_Elaborator.__init__` semantic sequence:
+
+1. Exact nominal document keys, supported schema, legacy/profile condition,
+   module identifier, and assignment of initial document/counter/profile state.
+2. Native type initialization with HIA-selected recursive-chain and
+   partial-record flags. This occurs before inspecting function inventory.
+3. Function inventory and creation of ordered function/signature/origin maps.
+4. For each function in source order: exact shape (v4 optional return_loans),
+   name, duplicate check, complete parameter admission, return-list kind,
+   resolution of **all** return references, then the stored-loan escape check.
+5. Native v4 origins, committing that origin row before checking effects.
+   Only after valid effects are the function and signature committed.
+6. Every concrete task declaration, including unused ones, in definition
+   order: resolve its name and admit its protocol against the complete registry.
+
+No host routine will inspect source names, decide schema/profile, check effects,
+walk return references, decide which declarations are tasks, resolve an origin
+path, or reconstruct a semantic lowering plan. The host will materialize the
+native-issued registry and type identities as representations of complete state.
+
+## Typed services and state
+
+The kernel requests only these separately owned native operations: initialize
+types; admit parameters; resolve one type; admit origins; admit a task protocol.
+Requests use monotonically increasing IDs, fixed kinds, exact resume phases,
+and full generic object streams. Parameters and returned descriptors use
+same-session issued IDs with bidirectional identity checks. Origins retain the
+native type owner's original parameter name and scalar offset.
+
+There is no raw-ID shortcut in the existing native type adapter. The new bridge
+will mechanically materialize native IDs into that session's exact descriptors
+and call its existing native APIs. This preserves the currently selected type
+owner's diagnostic policy: category, ordering and state remain contractual;
+some existing generalized English context differs from the older hosted types.
+Such dependency differences must not be relabeled constructor regressions.

+generic state result includes the detached document, native profile enum,
+initialization stage, registry rows, origin rows and semantic error status.
+Stage publication distinguishes no assigned fields, document/profile assigned,
+type owner assigned, and registry initialized. On semantic refusal the bridge
+mirrors only fields committed at that stage, including an origin row committed
+before a later effect error. Type-session cache/active/work state is retained.

+The completed state supplies `document`, `native_types`/`types`, zero initial
+serial/value slots, ordered `functions`, `signatures`, `return_origins`, and
+empty helpers/cache. The profile enum mechanically selects the existing static
+operation-set representation and returned-loan flag. The already implemented
+full-function session can then bind that same detached document and type state.
+The late function-owner installation hook remains after all constructor
+semantics, as in the current candidate.

+
+Use an independent constructor kernel and independent generic renderer image,
+with distinct state/request/frame identities. Reuse the existing generic

+# Complete native composite function owner
+
+This is an explicitly selected development candidate for the complete
+`_Elaborator.function` owner. It is not a cold-qualified release, an all-input
+equivalence proof, or whole-language/whole-stack closure. The constructor and
+outer `lower` still own their original hosted semantics. No old owner is removed.
+
+This document was reconstructed after the workspace restart. Its text is a new
+revision. The five semantic kernel sources/images and the bridge, codec,
+diagnostics, authoring bodies, ordinary wrapper, and terminator tests were
+recovered byte for byte from the independently frozen terminator evidence
+archive. The restored builder also matches its recorded pre-restart SHA.
+
+## Scope and ownership
+
+The retained function body contains 441 lines, 392 Python AST statements, 85
+conditionals, 23 loops and 56 explicit rejection sites. Its normalized original
+body is 27,110 bytes with SHA-256
+`b7336fb540911f220fef676d082c1a365d4712703ba5f08faeff3ac985913972`.
+Only its method name changes to `_reference_function`; the default path still
+uses that body. Selecting `HEPTA_HIA_COMPOSITE_FUNCTIONS_MANIFEST` requires the
+complete five-image bundle plus source-matching native types and task helpers.
+A selected native failure never falls back to hosted lowering.
+
+HIA owns both passes, declaration order, block/SSA maps, value consumption and
+external-loan flags, exact nominal type-ID comparisons, every record/enum/task/
+call/primitive operation, every terminator and match arm, generated names,
+value-slot accounting, helper-cache decisions, and the complete returned Core
+function. The adapter transports exact trees, forwards fixed native service
+requests, materializes generic output tokens and mirrors HIA-issued state. It
+does not inspect source instructions to plan or compute their lowering.
+
+The preserved entry contract is the ordinary verifier's bounded detached
+document and complete `lower()` path. The private `session.function(fn)` accepts
+only unchanged members of that document: it compares the full typed packet with
+the stored snapshot before sending native NEXT. A replacement object or mutation
+poisons the session. This custody check does not interpret types, SSA or CFG.
+Arbitrary private replacement dictionaries are therefore explicitly outside the
+compatibility claim. Direct private float-valued inputs are also outside it;
+the public snapshot gate rejects floats before this owner is reached.
+
+## Preserved order and state
+
+1. Each block is admitted for inventory, shape, name and duplicate status before
+   its parameters. Widths are reserved as a complete sum before flat names are
+   generated. Instructions then receive their original shape/profile/argument/
+   output-parameter checks.
+2. SSA names enter the global definition set only after that block's complete
+   first pass. A duplicate earlier in a block cannot hide a later type error.
+   All source blocks finish before entry/signature equality is checked.
+3. Pass two looks up all arguments before admitting the declared outputs.
+   Repeated `parameters` and `resolve` calls occur in their original order,
+   including the second primitive resolution in enum.tag and task.state.
+4. `reserve_values` updates the entire sum before testing 32,768. `fresh` tests
+   8,192 before incrementing. Partial counters remain observable on refusal.
+5. Match carries preserve environment insertion order, scalar-name alias
+   deduplication and the first occurrence's type. Case validation precedes
+   exhaustiveness, then variants lower in declaration order with original
+   edge/arm/drop/constant/decision/fresh sequencing.
+6. Helper-cache hits precede task-protocol checks. On a miss, the helper name
+   enters the cache after its first successful fresh allocation even if later
+   generation fails. Only a successful complete helper is appended.
+7. Every source function finishes before outer expanded inventories and final
+   primitive Core admission. The function owner does not move those gates.

+The session persists counters and numeric helper-cache identities across source
+functions. Per-function maps/IR are reset only after the complete stream and

+task-protocol checking and complete task-helper generation. HIA emits each
+request with a monotonic sequence, fixed kind and resume phase. The adapter

+replay, unissued IDs and invalid transport state poison the session; source
+semantic refusals preserve their original partial state.

+initialization but before the nominal constructor completes. Each native

+# Complete outer owner: finite transport and arena bounds
+
+These bounds apply to the ordinary public path: the existing structural
+verifier has detached a bounded source tree, the complete constructor has
+admitted it, and a fresh elaborator invokes outer lowering once. They do not
+grant execution authority or introduce a new source-language quota. The final
+primitive verifier retains its own full admission.
+
+Let `N <= 262144` be the existing source-node bound, `B <= 8388608` the existing
+source JSON byte bound, and `F <= 1024` the admitted source-function count.
+Native types issue at most 144 identities; the five task-helper operations are
+cached by issued nominal type and operation, so at most `H <= 720` successful
+helpers can be created. A failed helper creates no object handle. Every source
+occurrence is charged independently, including repeated names and references.
+
+## Initial packet
+
+The constructor's independent transport proof gives `40*N + B` for the complete
+document. The outer packet additionally carries an ordered registry with
+function names, parameter names/type IDs and return type IDs. It carries no
+expanded primitive slots or complete Core functions.
+
+An encoded registry function row has at most `88 + name_bytes` fixed framing;
+a parameter row at most `59 + name_bytes`; and a return identity at most 19
+bytes, since a decimal issued identity has at most three digits. Rounding these
+to 128 bytes per function occurrence, 80 per parameter occurrence and 32 per
+return occurrence is conservative. Those are disjoint original source nodes.
+Their copied name bytes are already charged within `B`. The registry outer
+list adds 24 bytes. Thus `registry <= 128*N + B + 24`.
+
+The six-item packet's surrounding list, zero serial, zero value count and two
+empty helper lists contribute 106 bytes. The complete bound is therefore
+`168*N + 2*B + 130 = 60817538` bytes, below the existing 64 MiB source region
+(`67108864`). This deliberately loose bound includes every repeated parameter
+or return; it does not assume shared strings or memoized admission.
+
+The initial HIA gate rejects non-fresh private owner histories. That private
+restriction is explicit; the ordinary public constructor produces exactly the
+fresh counters and empty helper inventories required here.
+
+## Native arena
+
+The 80 MiB workspace reserves the first 64 MiB plus 64 KiB for source and fixed
+state, leaving 16711680 bytes for arena allocations. Complete Core objects are
+held as opaque references outside this arena; HIA chooses their identities and
+the generic decoder substitutes only those issued objects.
+
+The source allocates a 17280-byte helper lease table, an `8*F` export pointer
+vector, two 32-byte lists, at most 160 bytes per function request, and 64 bytes
+per completed function reference. Exports add at most `64*F` bytes. A successful
+helper uses a 64-byte reference/list segment and a further 32-byte segment when
+appended to the final function list. The four-field envelope, short literal
+strings, schema choice and fixed lists fit within 1024 bytes. Header validation
+uses fixed state fields and allocates no arena nodes.
+
+The rounded charge `320*F + 128*H + 32768 <= 452608` bytes is therefore above all
+actual arena allocations and far below the available 16711680 bytes. Failed
+native continuations stop the same finite loops and allocate no unbounded retry
+history. The stream stack sees only the small envelope, lists and opaque leaf
+references, not the depths of expanded Core objects.
+
+## Late gates and large outputs
+
+HIA records each completed function's actual native block-list count, observes
+every helper's real metadata and exact output header, and waits for all source
+functions to complete. Only then does it apply the original 1024-function and
+4096-block final inventory gates. A later function error retains priority over
+an earlier function's excessive generated block count or a huge completed Core
+object. No intermediate 8 MiB limit is introduced.
+
+Successful complete Core objects are not serialized back through this fixed
+input packet. The final token stream contains their opaque identities in HIA's
+chosen order. The existing primitive verifier performs the final expanded
+program byte/node/type/control-flow admission after lowering finishes.
+
+These are source/arena bounds, not measured process RSS or a cold qualification.
+The borrowed 192 MiB function, 128 MiB type and 2 MiB helper buffers remain owned
+by their existing sessions. The temporary 80 MiB outer arena and 192 MiB
+constructor arena release on completion, refusal and partial allocation
+failure; the ordinary public boundary separately closes committed sessions.

+# Native Core emitter owner
+
+This owner moves all six original `_Emitter` method bodies in
+`hepta.hia_program_native` into a checked HIA continuation image:
+`__init__`, `ordered_blocks`, `label`, `function_symbol`, `wrapper`, and
+`render`. The original AST is preserved independently in
+the text fixture named `hia_program_emitter_v76.py.txt` in `tests/fixtures`.

+imports the authoring compiler or evaluates those original bodies.
+
+The HIA image owns the complete method control tables, branch decisions,
+generator suspension, foreign effect permissions, exception transitions,
+temporary retirement, and named-local retirement. The original source and
+compiler limits remain unchanged. The image is generated by
+`tools/generate_hia_core_emitter.py` and the finite authoring compiler in
+`tools/hia_core_emitter_control.py`.
+
+## Exact foreign keyword-call boundary
+
+The original constructor contains `Code(**code_options(machine_plan))`.
+Preparing that mapping and invoking `Code` are separate HIA-issued effects.
+The first services the actual CPython `DICT_MERGE` operation with the real
+callable still on its stack, preserving mapping protocol, duplicate-key and
+non-mapping diagnostics. HIA then retires the original temporary mapping.
+Only a separately claimed call transfers the prepared exact dictionary and
+callable into the interpreter operand stack. Holding that dictionary in a
+bridge local through the entire call would change the lifetime of its values.
+
+The representation port is a fixed straight-line opcode template for reviewed
+CPython 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 ABIs. Its call suffix is replaced by balanced stack
+pops and a return; it does not execute arbitrary source, owner policy, `eval`,
+`exec` or a runtime authoring compiler. A differing interpreter/opcode shape
+is rejected. This mechanism remains an explicit CPython runtime dependency.
+The physical-profile matrix is distinct from tests run on an actual version.
+
+Ordinary positional and named calls also transfer their temporary operands
+after HIA has granted the exact call permission. Borrowing those operands
+until the later acknowledgment can incorrectly delay a Python callee's
+parameter retirement, including the reversed named-local order in 3.14.
+The transfer is part of the fixed foreign call, and an interrupted
+acknowledgment still forbids replay.
+
+## Selection, custody, and proofs
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_CORE_EMITTER_MANIFEST` requests explicit selection. Each new public
+operation rereads and binds manifest, HIA source, and executable image bytes.
+`emit_program_machine` captures the selected owner, including captured
+absence, for the complete operation. A nested callback cannot replace that
+capability by changing the environment. The checker registry uses the actual
+captured executable owner; a later selector or backing file cannot rewrite
+the identity of an already admitted proof operation.
+
+Each effect requires its exact issued permission and a native claim. Effects
+and returned terminal values cannot be replayed. An interruption after a real
+effect but before storing its acknowledgment retains an unknown frame; it
+does not manufacture completion or grant another call.
+

+
+`tools/build_hia_core_emitter.py` requires a completed matching-source cold
+report before creating its output. The original compiler child limit remains
+20 seconds. A retained development compiler is never a cold qualification.

+module and the original 51 machine and 50 Core callers. Original IDs,

+## Boundary and retained implementation

+publication and the external Python operations requested by the HIA controller
+remain explicit dependencies. No whole-backend, default activation, global
+safety, universal semantic-equivalence or legacy-deletion claim follows from a
+selected component or its finite tests.

+The original PR888 implementation at
+`acffa9262f31d073f8f0a6f0201eae201039f619` used a literal pool and 31 HIA units.

+supply a host-generated table.
+
+## Continuation and physical object custody
+
+HIA issues every foreign primitive, exact request identity, native claim and
+acknowledgement. A callback permission is consumed before the fixed transport
+executes that callback. Reply loss or other unknown completion cannot authorize
+a duplicate effect. Real caught exceptions leave the capture handler before
+HIA-authorized temporary retirement and delivery of the exact exception through
+the shared CPython mechanism. An original error traceback retains the original
+named locals; it is not replaced with a fabricated native error.

+The observed transport profile admits exactly CPython 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 on the
+already required Linux x86-64 ABI. It does not guess the behavior of later
+versions or another Python implementation. HIA latches that word and rejects
+continuation drift. Live temporary operands retire in birth-order LIFO first;
+then named slots retire forwards for 3.12/3.13 and backwards for 3.14. Cell
+references are dropped without clearing a cell still held by a separate lazy
+generator. Non-cell temporary holes are skipped only after all temporary births
+are zero. Independent-VM controls compare every complete source, output and
+workspace buffer and surrounding canaries for all three explicit ABI words;
+this is not a claim to have run three actual interpreters.

+Facades prepare a native frame, transfer their formal parameter references, and
+only then drive it. The five default helper facades and four public Plan
+facades use ordinary fixed-arity calls with individual carrier pops so they do
+not retain another argument tuple across the original call. Actual controls
+include success and held-error paths, outer handled exceptions, weak-reference
+observations and later diagnostic traceback detachment. No garbage collection
+is used to hide an extra reference.

+separate from the explicit service-held owner inventory. A reviewed captured
+registry identifies each exact capability type and scope hook. A captured
+absence is different from no scope; a serialized dictionary or caller-supplied
+held tuple cannot override an ordinary ambient selector.

+and Plan before invoking foreign program verification. Plan and Core admission
+freshly read the manifest, source and executable, retain the actual immutable

+changes. After scope exit, a new proof consumer re-admits the current selector
+and rejects evidence for the prior selection. Tests use two valid mapped images
+with different bytes, not just changed digest metadata. The alternate NOP-suffix
+image is an identity fault control, not qualified compiler output.

+Actual composition controls forbid retained Code, ELF, Function/helper and
+selected Plan bodies; all six owners return actual machine frames. Initial

+# Fixed CPython note adapter emitted by HIA
+
+This development component replaces C compilation of the fixed exception note
+and delivery mechanism with an HIA packer. It retains the same hosted CPython
+3.14.4 ABI dependency; it does not establish whole normalization or whole HIA
+runtime qualification.
+
+The production input is `cpython_note_packer.hiaasm`. Its entry accepts an empty
+source buffer and emits a complete position independent machine image. Nonempty
+input is refused before writing output. A short output buffer is refused before
+any write. The generated image starts at offset zero, contains its own three
+fixed format strings, preserves SysV callee saved registers, aligns the stack
+for every indirect call, and uses no relocations, imports, dynamic loader, or
+global writable state.
+
+Runtime inputs are the already admitted four-pointer interpreter table, a real
+exception object, a fixed kind, borrowed container/key pointers, and a signed
+index. It rejects a null API table or exception, kinds outside 1..4, illegal
+indices, and nonnull container/key for delivery before touching interpreter
+error state. Kind 1 adds the mapping note, 2 the sequence note, and 3 the object
+note. Kind 4 gives the current raised slot one owned reference and returns NULL;
+the existing PYFUNCTYPE bridge propagates the actual exception. The mechanism
+does not traverse JSON, classify payloads, choose unwind order, repair Python
+exception chains, or change recursion limits.
+
+The Python generator is authoring support. The GNU assembly and linker script
+are independent test references. They are not production build dependencies.
+Before native packer compilation, an ordinary Core VM must compare every emitted
+byte with the independently assembled image, including all three strings and
+every branch displacement. Exact size, short output, nonempty source, refusal
+precedence, and output tail preservation are also checked. A retained compiler
+run, if performed, is development evidence only. Existing note, delivery,
+handled-exception, lifetime, and ACK controls remain required against the
+HIA-produced image; a byte match alone is not an all-input proof.
+
+Whole native delivery, default selection, live migration, and legacy deletion
+remain false until the separate completion gates actually pass.

+# Native enum-match lowering
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_ENUM_MATCH_MANIFEST` explicitly selects the HIA implementation of
+the complete `match` terminator responsibility in the ordinary nominal
+elaborator. The operator-owned manifest binds
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/enum_match.hiaasm`, its native image and its compiler
+digest. Submitted program bytes cannot choose this manifest. Selection failure,
+source mismatch, transport failure and semantic refusal never invoke the
+retained reference match implementation.
+
+The HIA owner validates match/case fields, source names and case arguments,
+exhaustiveness, duplicate cases and the prohibition against carrying a matched
+linear enum on its own case edge. It performs block lookup, nominal/primitive
+target-type comparison, duplicate linear-transfer checks and live-value
+preservation. It builds the deduplicated primitive carry inventory in the
+original environment order, excludes selected aliases from inactive padding,
+drops inactive owners, rejects inactive loans and emits the entire decision
+CFG, including the invalid-discriminant trap. Every generated name and the
+final fresh-name counter belong to HIA, including the counter after refusal.
+
+The bridge returns a complete Core first-block suffix and complete additional
+blocks. It does not interpret a lowering plan, look up cases, decide liveness,
+compute target types or create instructions. The ordinary caller copies those
+objects into the surrounding function. The complete primitive verifier still
+checks the result. This does not move ordinary record/enum construction, other
+operations, source/type admission, function orchestration, returned-loan entry
+binding, exports, the Agent, persistence or installation into this owner.
+Composite v1 still produces primitive v6, v2/v3 produce v7, and v4 produces v8.
+
+## Descriptor and identity custody
+
+The private packet is a typed, length-delimited tree:
+
+```text
+[serial, source_term, descriptors, environment, block_signatures]
+descriptor = [kind, primitive_flat_types, linear, [[variant, field_type_ids], ...]]
+environment_entry = [source_name, type_id, primitive_names, external, consumed]
+block_signature = [source_block_name, parameter_type_ids]
+```
+
+Both retained type owners intern every nominal descriptor within one
+elaboration: the hosted `_Types.cache` and the native session's HIA-issued
+descriptor graph. The adapter preserves that graph by Python object identity
+while holding every descriptor alive for the packet. It does not call Python
+type equality or hash a nominal identity. The HIA kernel compares nominal
+descriptor IDs directly. Primitive descriptors can be materialized separately;
+HIA compares their transported primitive names. No exponentially expanded
+nominal display key, object address or session token enters normalized Core.
+The packet is an internal representation of already admitted descriptors,
+not an alternate public type declaration interface. Mixing unrelated type
+sessions or inventing nominal descriptors does not acquire source admission.
+
+The image validates the private graph's representation before using it:
+descriptor and reference ranges, exact field inventories, primitive names,
+boolean flags, enum-flat/variant correspondence, buffer extents and safe output
+names. This does not replace the preceding type owner or decide source type
+declarations a second time. Source term checks and their first-error ordering
+remain the semantic responsibility of the match image.
+
+## Private bounds preserve the public profile
+
+The public document retains 8 MiB, 262,144 JSON value nodes and depth 64.
+Nominal elaboration retains 128 completed/active instantiations, 512 primitive
+slots per nominal layout, 32 enum variants, 64 fields per variant, 32,768
+elaborated value slots and 8,192 generated names. None of these limits is
+reduced by native selection.
+
+The private typed input allows 256 MiB, 8,388,608 nodes and depth 128. These
+are representation allowances, not larger public input limits. The private
+tree does not recursively expand record graphs: variants refer to descriptor
+IDs. A conservative node calculation uses `N = 262144`, `V = 32768`, and
+`D <= V + 128*511 + 128 = 98304` distinct held descriptors. Primitive
+descriptors used by environments/signatures consume the original value-slot
+budget; a retained enum's primitive field descriptors consume its 511
+non-tag slots. Zero-width nominal types remain interned and add no new
+primitive descriptor per source occurrence.
+
+| Packet part | Conservative typed-node bound |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Raw source term, including object keys | `2*N` |
+| Environment tuples and primitive names | `6*N + V` |
+| Block-signature tuples and parameters | `3*4096 + N` |
+| Descriptor graphs, flat arrays and variant fields | `6*D + 128*512 + 128*32*3 + 128*32*64` |
+| Root and inventory containers | `8` |
+| Total | `3,334,152` |
+
+This is below 8,388,608. Even charging 24 bytes per typed node, all copied
+128-byte environment/primitive/block/variant names, and the complete original
+8-MiB source-term text stays below 140 MiB; the 256-MiB allowance has additional
+room. The descriptor tree has at most seven container levels. A source term
+loses its original function/block ancestors when put in the packet, so the
+private depth-128 bound also preserves the public depth-64 profile. The
+validator checks its node/depth budgets independently from byte length.
+
+Scratch is 32 MiB. Fixed descriptor, environment, exact-name hash, mark,
+signature, carry and block tables occupy less than 12 MiB. The largest case
+hash occupies 4 MiB. All 32 target-edge vectors together need at most 8 MiB;
+the unchanged fresh-name quota bounds generated parameter vectors, and
+padding/instruction records occupy less than another 4 MiB. Hashes only locate
+table candidates: exact source bytes resolve collisions.
+
+Output is 64 MiB. A conservative private bound allows each of 32 arms to
+forward 32,768 primitive names, independently of how many names were freshly
+generated. Forwarded aliases do not all charge the fresh-name counter. These
+lists use less than 20 MiB; generated parameters, decisions, source names and
+at most 32*511 inactive-slot drops keep the complete output below 32 MiB.
+The 64-MiB output region therefore does not rely on an incorrectly assumed
+one-to-one relation between output occurrences and fresh names.
+
+All buffers are private to one call. The image reinitializes the scratch it
+uses; an earlier call does not establish initial state. Input bytes are checked
+unchanged after native return. Shared code is mapped read/execute only after
+copying. This trusted code selection is not an execution sandbox for arbitrary
+machine bytes and not a proof of all-input equivalence.
+
+## Output and refusal protocol
+
+The three-buffer HIA entry takes source/readbuf, output/mutbuf and
+workspace/mutbuf. A completed semantic result returns `64 + payload_length`.
+The eight little-endian u64 header words are:
+
+| Word | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| 0 | ASCII `HIAMAT01` |
+| 1 | Zero, or a declared semantic error ID |
+| 2 | Final fresh-name counter |
+| 3 | Payload byte length |
+| 4–7 | Zero |
+
+Success payloads contain exactly `first` and `blocks`.
+`first` contains exactly `ops` and `term`; `blocks` contains the complete
+generated Core block objects in the original order. Refusals contain
+`{"first":null,"blocks":null}` and retain the precise final counter. The
+adapter checks framing, reserved words, extent, counter correlation and object
+envelopes. It materializes the declared original error code/message; unknown
+statuses or malformed results refuse rather than permitting fallback.
+
+## Validation and evidence scope
+
+`tests/test_hia_enum_match_native.py` verifies checked-in source reproduction
+and the unchanged compiler limits, then executes the actual native image.
+The retained `_reference_match` algorithm is an independent oracle over real
+ordinary elaborator environments, with original reference edge closures and
+fresh counters. It compares the full generated CFG, first errors and counters,
+including late target failures, duplicate/omitted linear values, permuted
+cases, scalar aliases, all 32 variants and exhaustion during name generation.
+
+Ordinary comparisons cover all four composite versions and require byte-exact
+normalized Core with the reference match method disabled on the selected run.
+Independent VM runs check results, allocation refusal and owner/loan balance.
+Actual emitted machine programs use allocator/free wrappers and an invalid-tag
+abort control. Private loan-padding descriptors are explicitly synthetic ABI
+controls, not accepted source programs. Large repeated zero-width and scalar
+target fixtures exercise representation growth without lowering public limits.
+Canary, short-buffer, changed-input and concurrent-call controls cover the
+native boundary. A real installed-wheel test forbids authoring-module imports
+and the reference owner, and requires missing/changed installed source or an
+invalid manifest to refuse.
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_ENUM_MATCH_DEVELOPMENT_MANIFEST` is a test-only image reuse option.
+It cannot be combined with `HEPTA_HIA_ENUM_MATCH_COLD_REPORT`. A cold report
+must bind the complete current source contract and all original qualification
+gates before the shared `enum-match` builder publishes a manifest. Development
+execution and old compiler reuse do not qualify a changed source tree, replace
+whole-language acceptance, activate a deployment or authorize retiring other
+production owners.

+elaborator. The operator-owned manifest binds
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/enum_operations.hiaasm`, its image and compiler digest.
+Submitted source cannot select a manifest. A selected image, source, transport

+HIA owns exact attribute admission, declared enum-output checks, variant names
+and selection, payload type comparison, ordered linear consumption, fresh-name

+adapter copies complete instruction objects, consumption flags, bindings and
+the fresh-name counter. It does not interpret an instruction-generation plan.

+oracle and as the unselected route. Selection is explicit, not a claim that
+the entire elaborator has moved to HIA. Source/function orchestration, the
+preceding argument/name checks, the type owner, record operations, tasks,
+ordinary calls, primitive operations and the final primitive verifier retain
+their existing boundaries. Enum match has a separate native selector. Public
+composite v1 still lowers to primitive v6, v2/v3 to v7 and v4 to v8.

+## Exact type-owner ordering
+
+The enclosing function resolves instruction arguments and declared outputs
+before reaching either enum branch. This work remains before native entry.
+`enum.make` requires no additional type-owner calls. `enum.tag` originally
+resolves primitive `u32`, reparses its output declaration, checks output types,
+and only after success resolves the type used in the resulting binding.
+
+The HIA owner preserves this sequence with bounded continuations:
+
+| Phase | HIA decision and permitted following action |
+| --- | --- |
+| 0 | Check empty attributes and one enum argument. On success request 1. |
+| 1 | Receive `resolve("u32")` and the reparsed output declaration; perform exact output equality. On success request 2. |
+| 2 | Receive the final `resolve("u32")` result; bind that exact descriptor to the original primitive tag name. |
+
+Only the HIA request triggers each call to the existing type owner. The bridge
+does not compare types or decide whether output checking succeeded. A type
+owner's exception propagates at the original point. Refusal before a request
+does not call that owner, and mismatched output types never trigger the final
+resolve. The adapter rejects skipped, repeated or effect-producing requests.
+Tag operations never change the fresh-name counter or consume their argument.

+## Partial effects and independent identity
+
+An enum construction can fail after consuming a prefix of its arguments or
+emitting a prefix of its padding. Reusing one linear source twice consumes the
+first occurrence before rejecting the second. A buffer padding slot creates
+its size constant, owner name and success name in that order; a fresh-name
+failure can occur between those steps. Native results include these partial
+effects, and the caller applies them before raising the original error.
+
+The private packet holds each original value object once and stores every
+argument occurrence separately. Repeated aliases therefore share the same
+consumption flag without duplicating their flattened data. The packet also
+holds existing nominal descriptors by identity. Both retained type owners
+intern nominal descriptors within one elaboration. HIA compares nominal IDs,
+and compares separately materialized primitive descriptors by primitive name.
+No Python semantic equality, nominal display-key expansion or object address
+is used to decide equality in the selected path. HIA-issued types and hosted
+types follow the same packet representation.
+
+```text
+[phase, serial, operation, attributes, descriptors, values, arguments,
+ declared_outputs, expected_tag_type, reparsed_tag_outputs, bound_tag_type]
+descriptor = [kind, primitive_flat_types, linear, [[variant, field_type_ids], ...]]
+value = [type_id, primitive_names, external, consumed]
+argument = [source_name, value_id]
+declared_output = [source_name, type_id]
+```
+
+This is an internal representation of admitted types, not another public type
+declaration format. The HIA image validates exact packet inventories, types,
+indices, enum-flat correspondence, safe names, boolean flags, phase fields
+and buffer sizes before semantic work. It validates private typed node and
+depth budgets independently from byte length.

+## Private capacity preserves public limits
+
+Public source remains bounded by 8 MiB, 262,144 JSON value nodes and depth 64.
+Nominal elaboration still allows 128 completed/active instantiations, 512
+primitive slots per nominal layout, 32 variants, 64 fields per variant, 32,768
+elaborated value slots and 8,192 fresh names. These limits are unchanged.

+The private packet allows 256 MiB, 8,388,608 typed nodes and depth 128. Let
+`N = 262144` and `V = 32768`. A conservative bound on held descriptors is

+output inventory share the original value-slot quota; reparsing tag outputs
+can materialize at most another `V` primitive descriptors. Nominal descriptors
+are interned, including zero-width types. Primitive enum-field descriptors
+contribute at most 511 per enum. Two additional descriptors cover tag resolves.
+The private table permits 262,144 descriptors, so this does not narrow source.
+
+| Packet component | Conservative typed-node bound |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Raw attributes, including object keys | `2*N` |
+| Held values and their primitive names | `5*N + V` |
+| Argument occurrences | `3*N` |
+| Initial and reparsed declared outputs | `6*N` |
+| Descriptor graph, flats, variants and fields | `6*D + 128*512 + 128*32*3 + 128*32*64` |
+| Root and inventory containers | `32` |
+| Total | `5,353,516` |
+
+Charging 24 bytes per typed node uses less than 123 MiB. Even additionally
+charging four complete public 8-MiB payloads for attributes, argument names
+and repeated declarations, 128 bytes per held primitive name, every variant
+name and all primitive/kind strings keeps the private packet below 192 MiB.
+The 256-MiB buffer therefore has room beyond this conservative bound. The
+descriptor graph uses IDs instead of recursive descriptor expansion. Its
+container depth is bounded independently, and relocated attributes lose
+their source ancestors; the private depth-128 validator preserves depth-64
+public inputs.

+Scratch is 16 MiB. Fixed descriptor/value/consumption tables and operation

+zero-width arguments and declared outputs.
+
+Each call uses private buffers. The image initializes used state, checks

+native code mapped executable after copying; these bounds are not a sandbox
