+# Native record construction, unpack and projection
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_RECORD_OPERATIONS_MANIFEST` explicitly selects the HIA owner of the
+complete `record.make`, `record.unpack` and `record.get` branches in ordinary
+nominal lowering. The operator-owned manifest binds
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/record_operations.hiaasm`, its image and compiler digest.
+Program bytes cannot select the manifest. A selected source/image/transport
+or semantic refusal never invokes the retained reference branch.
+
+These three operations originally emit structural aliases rather than new
+primitive instructions. The HIA owner therefore returns their complete value
+bindings and consumption state, with an empty instruction sequence and the
+unchanged fresh-name counter. The bridge copies that result; it does not
+compute field offsets, compare types, flatten arguments, derive external-loan
+flags or implement an alias-generation plan.
+
+| Operation | Complete native responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| `record.make` | Exact attributes and nominal output kind, ordered field-type equality, ordered linear consumption, complete flattened aliases, and the original external flag. |
+| `record.unpack` | Exact attributes and input kind, output type/arity equality after the original reparse, consumption of the record, ordered field slices, exact field descriptors and inherited external flags. |
+| `record.get` | Exact attributes and input kind, field-name validation and lookup, partial-record token offset, uninitialized versus unknown field errors, prohibition against copying linear fields, output equality and the complete field alias. |
+
+The preceding source/name/argument admission, nominal type owner, function
+orchestration, return-origin handling and final primitive verifier retain their
+existing boundaries. Other record operations, including `record.borrow` and
+partial-record transitions, are separate responsibilities. Reading an
+initialized scalar field of a partial record is included in `record.get`;
+creating or changing that partial record is not moved by this owner. Enum and
+match owners have separate selectors. This does not claim a native rewrite of
+the whole elaborator or the rest of the system. Composite v1 still produces
+primitive v6, v2/v3 produce v7, and v4 produces v8.
+
+## Observable state and error order
+
+`record.make` checks every field's type before consuming any argument. It then
+consumes arguments in source order. Reusing a linear value consumes the first
+occurrence and rejects the second, preserving that partial state without
+creating an output binding. The native caller applies the returned consumption
+flags before raising the original error.
+
+The construction's external flag remains exactly
+`all(argument.external or not argument.type.linear) and not output.type.owns`.
+An empty record consequently has `external=true`. A record carrying a local
+loan does not become external merely because it owns no buffer. Unpacking
+propagates the input record's external flag to every field. Projection always
+creates the original non-external binding and refuses every linear field,
+including externally supplied loan fields.
+
+The original unpack and get branches reparse output declarations after their
+semantic guards. HIA preserves that point with one continuation. Phase 0
+checks attributes, operands and, for projection, field/loan policy. Only a
+successful native request triggers the existing type owner's
+`parameters(ins["out"])`. Phase 1 receives those descriptors, performs type and
+arity comparison in HIA, then consumes/binds. A type-owner exception propagates
+at its original point. Failed field lookup or linear projection never triggers
+the reparse. The adapter rejects skipped/repeated continuations, changed
+consumption during a request, nonempty primitive operations and any changed
+fresh-name counter.
+
+Bindings retain the exact descriptor used by the original branch: construction
+uses the initially declared record, while unpack/get use the record's field
+descriptor. The reparsed primitive descriptor is used for equality, not silently
+substituted for the bound field descriptor. Differential tests compare these
+object identities, complete aliases, external/consumed flags and type-owner
+call traces.
+
+## Private representation and descriptor custody
+
+```text
+[phase, serial, operation, attributes, descriptors, values, arguments,
+ initial_declared_outputs, reparsed_outputs]
+descriptor = [kind, primitive_flat_types, linear, [[field_name, type_id], ...], base_record_id_or_null]
+value = [type_id, primitive_names, external, consumed]
+argument = [source_name, value_id]
+declared_output = [source_name, type_id]
+```
+
+The bridge holds each input value object once and retains every argument
+occurrence separately. Aliases share one consumption flag without repeatedly
+copying their flattened names. It also holds nominal descriptors by object
+identity. Both existing type owners intern nominal and partial descriptors
+within one elaboration. HIA compares nominal IDs directly and primitive
+descriptors by primitive name. Neither Python type equality nor an expanded
+nominal display key decides equality on the selected path.
+
+Record fields and partial-record base descriptors use IDs, so a shared
+zero-width type graph does not recursively expand. Enum/task fields need only
+their existing kind, flat layout and linear flag. This private graph represents
+already admitted types and is not a public alternative type declaration format.
+The HIA image validates exact inventories, indices, safe names, booleans,
+primitive names, record-flat correspondence and the partial-record buffer
+token/base kind before semantic access.
+
+## Capacity without a smaller public language
+
+The public limits remain 8 MiB of source, 262,144 JSON value nodes, depth 64,
+128 completed/active nominal instantiations, 512 primitive layout slots,
+64 record fields, 32,768 elaborated value slots and 8,192 fresh names.
+These operations remain legal at serial 8,192 when they need no fresh names.
+
+The private typed tree permits 256 MiB, 8,388,608 nodes and depth 128. Let
+`N = 262144` and `V = 32768`. Held descriptors are bounded by
+`D <= 2*V + 128*64 + 128 = 73856`: actual values and initially declared outputs
+share the value-slot quota; the one output reparse can materialize another
+`V` primitive descriptors; each interned record contributes at most 64
+primitive field descriptors. Zero-width nominal descriptors remain interned.
+The descriptor/value tables each allow 262,144 entries.
+
+| Packet component | Conservative typed-node bound |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Raw attributes, including object keys | `2*N` |
+| Held values and primitive names | `5*N + V` |
+| Argument occurrences | `3*N` |
+| Initial and reparsed output inventories | `6*N` |
+| Descriptor rows, flats and fields | `7*D + 128*512 + 3*128*64` |
+| Root and inventory containers | `32` |
+| Total | `4,834,208` |
+
+Charging 24 bytes per node uses less than 111 MiB. Four complete public
+8-MiB payload allowances cover attributes, argument names and repeated output
+declarations. An additional 128 bytes per held primitive name, every field
+name and all kind/primitive strings still keeps the packet below 192 MiB.
+The 256-MiB limit therefore has room beyond the conservative bound. Descriptor
+references prevent recursive expansion; relocated source attributes lose
+their function/block ancestors. Private depth 128 preserves public depth 64.
+The native validator checks byte length, node count and depth separately.
+
+Scratch is 16 MiB. Fixed tables/state occupy 6,303,744 bytes, and all dynamic
+binding records and alias vectors fit in a further 16 KiB: at most 64 bindings
+and 512 copied primitive names. Output is 8 MiB. Even `N` consumption flags,
+64 long output names and 512 long primitive names fit below 2 MiB. These bounds
+include bad public arities that reach branch checks; they do not assume only
+successful source instructions arrive.
+
+Each invocation owns its source/output/workspace buffers. The image initializes
+used scratch and checks bounds; the bridge verifies unchanged source after
+return. Trusted selected code is copied before executable mapping. This is
+not a sandbox for arbitrary machine bytes or a proof of all-input equivalence.
+
+## Protocol and evidence controls
+
+The entry takes source/readbuf, output/mutbuf and workspace/mutbuf. A completed
+result returns `64 + payload_length`. Its eight little-endian u64 header words
+are magic `HIAREC01`, semantic error, unchanged serial, continuation request,
+payload length and three reserved zeros. Representation/ABI failure returns
+`0xfffffff1`. The JSON result contains exactly `ops`, `consumed` and `values`.
+Errors and requests have no bindings. Successful construction/projection has
+one binding; successful unpack has zero through 64. All bindings are complete
+and initially unconsumed; `ops` is always empty.
+
+`tests/test_hia_record_operations_native.py` covers exact checked-source
+generation and unchanged compiler limits, all four composite schemas, original
+branch/state/type-call differentials, every public branch error, duplicate
+linear arguments, nominal identity, empty/nested aliases and external loans.
+It checks initialized/uninitialized partial fields, returned-loan origin
+preservation, partial tasks, maximum-width records and exact value-slot limits.
+Independent HIA VM and actual image bytes are compared across continuation
+phases. Combined native type, record, enum and match owners run with their
+reference implementations disabled. Actual machine allocator/refusal/free
+controls, short buffers, canaries, excessive depth and concurrency exercise
+the executable boundary. A real installed wheel runs with authoring imports
+and reference record operations disabled, and rejects missing/modified source
+or invalid manifests.
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_RECORD_OPERATIONS_COLD_REPORT` requests a matching-source cold
+fixture. `HEPTA_HIA_RECORD_OPERATIONS_DEVELOPMENT_MANIFEST` explicitly selects
+development evidence; supplying both is an error. Default bootstrapped fixtures
+are labelled `BOOTSTRAP_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY`. A pinned predecessor compiler used
+for development does not qualify the current whole source tree. Shared source
+contract/workflow integration, current-source cold qualification and retirement
+of remaining owners are separate gates.

+
+`HEPTA_HIA_RECORD_TRANSITIONS_MANIFEST` explicitly selects the complete HIA
+owner of `record.begin`, `record.take`, `record.insert`, `record.finish`,

+source, transport and semantic failures never invoke the reference branches.

+ordinary record operation. Enum construction/tag and match retain their own
+native selectors. The enclosing SSA/function/call/task orchestration, type
+owner, returned-loan origin processing and final primitive verifier retain
+their existing responsibilities. Completing these record branches is not a
+claim that all ordinary lowering or the complete system has been rewritten.
+Composite versions and their primitive normalization targets are unchanged.
+In particular, earlier profiles do not gain partial-record operations merely
+because an image is selected.

+| `record.insert` | Input/field/type checks, duplicate-initialization rejection, declaration-ordered initialized inventory, output comparison, ordered consumption and complete token/field aliases. |
+| `record.finish` | Complete initialized-field equality, output comparison, consumption, token drop and complete record binding. |
+| `record.abandon` | Empty initialized inventory, empty-output comparison, consumption and token drop. |
+| `record.borrow` | Exact field/mode inventory, mode validation before field lookup, primitive owner/view eligibility, output comparison, complete primitive borrow operation and exact loan binding. |

+not choose initialized fields, calculate field offsets, decide linearity,
+generate fresh names or interpret an instruction-generation plan. Every new
+binding keeps the original descriptor and begins with `external=false` and
+`consumed=false`. The final primitive verifier still checks actual capability
+relationships, including suspension, exclusivity and borrowing during moves.

+## Existing type-owner continuations

+The surrounding function already resolves source arguments and initially
+declared output types before entering a branch. HIA preserves every later
+type-owner call at its original point. A query carries data selected by HIA;
+the bridge dispatches the existing method and transports its result.

+| Operation | Query order after native semantic guards |
+| --- | --- |
+| `begin` | No further type-owner call. |
+| `take` | `partial_record(base, remaining_fields)`, then `parameters(ins["out"])`. |
+| `insert` | `partial_record(base, initialized_fields_in_declaration_order)`, then output reparse. |
+| `finish`, `abandon` | Output reparse only. |
+| `borrow` | `resolve("readbuf" or "mutbuf")`, then output reparse. |

+construction/resolution, and phase 2 after output reparse. Request 1 carries a
+base descriptor ID and HIA-generated field names, request 2 carries the loan

+from phase 0 to phase 2. The adapter rejects skipped, repeated and reordered
+requests. Requests have no instructions, bindings, changed consumption flags
+or changed fresh-name counter.

+base, ordered field names and field types before continuing. The type owner

+output-type refusal, exactly as in the original implementation. Tests restore

+The native result includes effects accumulated before a semantic refusal, and
+the caller applies them before raising. Taking a whole record consumes it,
+creates its partial token and moves every primitive owner in field order.
+A counter refusal between buffer-token names or between nested owner moves
+therefore retains the original consumption flags, instruction prefix and final
+counter. A field binding is created only after all of its moves succeed.

+# Native release selection, rollback and restart observation
+
+`hia-select` is an explicit Linux x86-64 executable. HIA owns argument
+admission, durable selection bytes, the sequence/current compare-and-swap,
+previous-release rollback, metadata identity policy and JSON receipts. A fixed
+syscall adapter holds the root, lock and state descriptors, captures bytes,
+performs atomic publication and reports syscall outcomes. HIA SHA-256 computes
+both package and selection-record digests. No Python, libc, dynamic interpreter
+or child executable is required at runtime.
+
+Before either mutation, the application runs the **actual immutable-release
+verifier** against the operator-supplied package and its pinned target hash.
+It embeds the unchanged `release_install_policy.hiaasm` and `sha256_stream`
+images. The selection generator mechanically includes the installer's existing
+package capture/hash, safe root traversal, installed directory/file readback,
+exact directory inventory and identity checks. It does not substitute a file
+existence test, accept a selected source manifest on trust or execute a helper
+process. Tests check exact shared verifier bytes and exercise real installed
+release corruption.
+
+This adds the release-selection owner. It does not replace the default `hia`
+CLI, change a running service, migrate the Agent journal, grant a release any
+execution authority, remove old releases, recover abandoned stage files or
+prove that the package's executable bytes are qualified HIA. It does not close
+whole-native product delivery. The authoring and source-bound build driver
+remain hosted bootstrap/custody components.
+
+## Explicit operator interface
+
+```sh
+python -B -m tools.build_hia_release_selection \
+  --compiler /qualified/B3.image.bin --cold-report /completed-current-cold.json \
+  --output /new/private/selection
+
+/new/private/selection/hia-select status /absolute/private/releases
+/new/private/selection/hia-select activate /absolute/private/releases 0 - TARGET_SHA256 < target.hiapack
+/new/private/selection/hia-select activate /absolute/private/releases 1 CURRENT_SHA256 NEXT_SHA256 < next.hiapack
+/new/private/selection/hia-select rollback /absolute/private/releases 2 NEXT_SHA256 CURRENT_SHA256 < target.hiapack
+```
+
+`status` takes only a root and never reads stdin. It observes sequence, current
+and previous selection without creating a lock or selection file, changing
+modes, renaming, fsyncing or executing a release. Its `release_verified:false`
+is intentional: observing selection metadata does not freshly inspect the
+selected package's contents. Use the installer's explicit `verify` with the
+original pinned package for that independent observation.
+
+A mutation requires a canonical unsigned decimal expected sequence and exact
+expected current identity. Sequence zero requires `-`; every positive sequence
+requires 64 lowercase hexadecimal bytes. Target identity is always 64 lowercase
+hexadecimal bytes. The stdin package has the unchanged 64 MiB inclusive ceiling,
+256-file limit, safe entry syntax, exact modes and exact exhaustion checks of
+the immutable installer. Hash or argument refusal precedes filesystem changes.
+
+The root has the installer's same existing-directory, effective-owner,
+permission and no-symlink traversal contract. The root and target release must
+already exist. A supplied package cannot choose the root or mutate its installed
+release. Selection metadata lives directly in the held root, separately from
+every content-addressed release directory.
+
+## Native state and transition policy
+
+The selected object is the ordinary file `.hia-selection.current`, not a
+symlink or executable dispatch shim. It has exact mode `0400`, the effective
+UID, one link and exactly 192 bytes. Its little-endian record is:
+
+| Bytes | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| 0–7 | `HIASEL01` |
+| 8–15 | Sequence, 1 through `2^64-1` |
+| 16–23 | Last action: 1 activate, 2 rollback |
+| 24–31 | Reserved zero |
+| 32–95 | Current release hash, 64 lowercase ASCII hexadecimal bytes |
+| 96–159 | Previous release hash; all zero bytes only at sequence 1 |
+| 160–191 | Raw SHA-256 of bytes 0–159 |
+
+Absent state means sequence 0 and no current or previous release. A present
+empty, truncated, oversized, malformed, changed-identity or checksum-invalid
+record refuses; it never becomes a fabricated empty state. Sequence 1 must be
+an activation with no predecessor. Later records require a different valid
+previous hash. Unknown versions and reserved fields refuse.
+
+`activate` requires both expected values to match current state, refuses a
+no-op target, increments the sequence by exactly one and records the old
+current as previous. `rollback` additionally requires the target to equal the
+recorded previous release; it is a single-step reversible selection and records
+the replaced current as the new previous. It cannot invent historical release
+history or roll sequence 1 back to absence. Both operations refuse sequence
+exhaustion rather than wrapping. Every rollback target is independently
+package-verified again before publication.
+
+The protocol provides a monotonically increasing sequence within the retained
+local state. It does not claim freshness when an administrator restores the
+entire root and its selection metadata together. An external anti-rollback
+anchor or historical request journal is a separate responsibility.
+
+## Serialization and publication
+
+`.hia-selection.lock` is an ordinary zero-byte file, exact mode `0600`, owned by
+the effective UID with one link. Mutations may create it with their own private
+`0077` umask. Status only opens an existing lock; if the lock is absent but a
+state file exists, it refuses that incoherent observation. No lock file is ever
+removed or replaced by this program.
+
+The kernel's nonblocking `flock` serializes cooperating mutators with an
+exclusive lock and status readers with a shared lock. A busy lock returns exit
+18; it is not a queued mutation or a success. The held lock inode is compared
+to its name after acquisition and before and after publication. Process death
+releases the kernel lock without stale-PID ownership inference.
+
+Under the exclusive lock, the native application:
+
+1. Reads and checks existing state and the expected sequence/current pair.
+2. Runs complete actual installed-release verification against captured input.
+3. Creates a random, exclusive, nofollow `.hia-selection-stage-…` file containing
+   only the new HIA-produced record. It fixes its mode to `0400`, fsyncs the
+   file, and checks its inode, size, mode, owner and named identity.
+4. Rechecks the named old state and the held lock. Initial publication uses
+   `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`; a successor atomically replaces only the
+   previously checked selection metadata while the exclusive lock is held.
+5. Fsyncs the root directory, reopens the new state, checks its full checksum,
+   bytes and published inode, rechecks the root and lock, then writes a receipt.
+
+Installed release files are never opened for writing or renamed. The program
+never creates a `current` symlink or changes another installation. Failed or
+interrupted private stages remain for a separately authorized administrative
+recovery operation; a prefix is not treated as deletion authority.
+
+The lock is advisory and the root belongs to the same operating-system user.
+These checks establish point-in-time observations and serialization among this
+protocol's cooperating processes. They do not protect against a hostile same-UID
+writer ignoring the lock, later changes after readback, compromised kernels or
+all possible storage-device power-loss behavior. Inode/time changes detected
+during the actual operation refuse without silently overwriting release data.
+
+## Receipts, failed acknowledgments and restart
+
+A successful activation returns, for example:
+
+```json
+{"schema":"hepta.hia.release-selection.v1","operation":"activate","sequence":1,"current":"...","previous":null,"release_verified":true}
+```
+
+The sequence and selected hashes are actual readback, not a planned future
+state. A successful status has `operation:"status"` and
+`release_verified:false`. Writes retry `EINTR`; a complete receipt write is
+required for exit 0. Receipt output is not an atomic transaction with the
+selection state.
+
+If stdout fails or the process dies after rename, selection may already have
+changed. Root-fsync failure can also leave a visible new state without the
+operation having established durable success. A new `status` invocation reads
+what exists after restart. Compare the observed sequence/current/previous to
+the attempted transition. Reissuing the old expected sequence cannot apply the
+transition again: it returns a conflict. Do not invent a new expected sequence
+merely to turn an uncertain request into a new action.
+
+Status provides current-state resolution. It is not a historical receipt API:
+after further successful transitions it cannot attribute every earlier lost
+acknowledgment to an individual request. The Agent's historical operation
+journal and deployed Runtime continuity remain separate owners.
+
+| Exit | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| 0 | Requested observation/mutation and complete receipt write succeeded |
+| 10 | Root, state, lock or release object type/mode/owner/link/extent refusal |
+| 11 | Package bytes/hash/inventory or state content/checksum refusal |
+| 12 | Observed inode/time identity changed |
+| 14 | Private stage creation or atomic publication failed |
+| 15 | Mapping, descriptor, synchronization or receipt I/O failure |
+| 16 | Argument or internal policy-state refusal |
+| 17 | Input package exceeds 64 MiB |
+| 18 | Kernel lock busy |
+| 19 | Expected sequence/current conflict or no-op activation |
+| 20 | Rollback target is not the recorded previous release |
+| 21 | Sequence exhausted |
+| 64 | Wrong argument count |
+
+A failure exit is not proof of no filesystem effect. Original observations and
+failures must remain attached to the actual source and execution identity.
+
+## Qualification
+
+`ReleaseSelectionSourceTests` executes an independent Core VM before any native
+seed for argument conversion, canonical sequence bounds, exact state bytes,
+checksum comparison, CAS, rollback, exhaustion, receipts and all ELF packer
+bytes. It preserves the language's existing return/list budgets by observing
+long receipt bytes in bounded independent views.
+
+`ReleaseSelectionKernelTests` builds a real B0/B1/B2 fixed point for explicitly
+labelled development, or requires the current completed cold report when
+`HEPTA_HIA_RELEASE_SELECTION_COLD_REPORT` is supplied. It uses the actual native
+installer, real immutable releases, independent record decoding, contention,
+two process CAS, truncation/corruption, symlinks/hard links, modes and release
+readback. `ReleaseSelectionFaultTests` requires actual `strace` fault injection
+for stage/root fsync failures, lost stdout acknowledgment, `EINTR`, and SIGKILL
+before and after publication. Missing ptrace access is a failed environment
+observation, not a skipped or passed native qualification.
+
+The source-bound builder refuses missing or stale complete cold manifests before
+creating its output directory and rechecks all original sources/images/report
+bytes before publishing. Passing a development test does not qualify a later
+merged source, activate a default CLI, migrate a live worker or authorize
+retiring an unported production owner.

+# Native HIA request journal owner
+
+This component replaces the request journal decisions in `HIAAgentService.call`
+when `HEPTA_HIA_REQUEST_JOURNAL_MANIFEST` selects an admitted image. HIA owns
+request-key admission, exact durable row binding, replay validation custody,
+one dispatch, returned-response custody, terminal completion, and transaction
+cleanup claims. The original `main.requests` table and its SQLite database and
+WAL remain the durable authority. No second journal, schema migration, row
+reset, new-key retry, or inferred completion receipt is introduced.
+
+The default service retains its independent original implementation in
+`HIAAgentService._call_reference`. The selected implementation does not call
+that implementation. SQLite, filesystem access, tool handlers, canonical JSON
+and digest formation, and the Python object bridge remain foreign operations.
+This is a bounded owner replacement, not a claim that the complete Agent or
+production stack has become HIA-native.
+
+## Source and runtime custody
+
+| Responsibility | Source |
+| --- | --- |
+| Retained policy, transition rules, byte bounds, tokens and cleanup epochs | `examples/hia_bootstrap/request_journal.hiaasm` |
+| Reproducible authoring source | `tools/generate_hia_request_journal.py` |
+| Fixed SQL transport and guarded callback connection | `hepta/hia_request_journal_native.py` |
+| Actual caller integration | `hepta/hia_agent_service.py`, `hepta/hia_agent_store.py` |
+| Strict source-matched native build | `tools/build_hia_request_journal.py` |
+| VM, actual machine, SQLite, process-exit and installed-wheel controls | `tests/test_hia_request_journal_native.py` |
+
+The assembly is a packaged native source resource. Runtime admission binds
+the selected manifest, image bytes and installed source hash. Invalid selected
+admission fails before `AgentStore` creates or opens a state directory. The
+installed wheel runs without importing `tools`, and the installed-wheel
+control poisons the original request dispatcher and execution-budget constructors.
+
+The image operates on one retained mutable state per request. State is not
+recreated from Python flags for each decision. The checksum covers the state
+header, identity bytes and active response bytes. This detects accidental
+corruption and inconsistent transport; it does not authenticate a buffer
+against malicious code running in the same process and able to recompute the
+checksum. Host effects and cooperating SQLite writers remain trusted parts
+of the adapter boundary.
+
+## Original journal and transaction ordering
+
+The existing six-column row remains unchanged:
+
+```text
+main.requests(key, digest, tool, state, response, started_ns)
+```
+
+HIA validates the exact key, request digest, tool, state, response presence,
+timestamp and response bytes at the relevant transitions. Every fixed journal
+statement explicitly names `main.requests`; a TEMP table cannot become request
+authority. Inserts and completion updates require a real affected-row count of
+one and an exact row readback before COMMIT. Completion uses a conditional
+update over the original key, digest, tool, running state, null response and
+original timestamp.
+
+The selected adapter opens a dedicated connection to the same existing
+database with `mode=rw`, WAL and `synchronous=FULL`. It retains the official
+`AgentStore.db` object, main-file identity, WAL and shared-memory identities,
+and creator PID. Replacement, symlink, ownership or writable-mode drift
+refuses before request SQL. The official connection remains an ordinary
+attribute with its original setter behavior. The private connection cannot
+borrow an already active transaction from either connection.
+
+For a new eligible key, native admission emits BEGIN, row read, running-intent
+INSERT, exact readback and COMMIT. Dispatch is legal only after that commit is
+confirmed. Existing rows have three distinct outcomes:
+
+* A different request digest conflicts with the original key binding.
+* A noncompleted row remains unknown; admission never reexecutes that request.
+* A completed row supplies its exact stored response to replay validation.
+  Validation and its final COMMIT must be acknowledged before replay bytes can
+  be returned. Verification-proof replay still validates its retained scope
+  inside the original request-read transaction.
+
+Ordinary handlers run after the durable intent. Their returned or known-error
+response must first enter the HIA confirmed-result phase. The original cost
+ledger write still occurs before the ordinary terminal-response transaction.
+HIA then opens a new private transaction, validates the original running row,
+updates the exact response, checks readback and requires confirmed COMMIT.
+
+For `hia_adopt` and `hia_rollback`, HIA opens the private effect transaction and
+revalidates the original running row before emitting dispatch authority. Slot,
+version and artifact-index changes, plus the exact terminal response, use that
+same connection and transaction. They commit together. A known handler error
+can produce a rejected response only after confirmed rollback of this effect
+transaction; the rejected response then receives a separate completion
+transaction. An unknown rollback or commit never manufactures a rejection.
+
+The completed atomic path accepts a subsequent `finish` only as exact-byte
+idempotent readback. It emits no new SQL. A replayed ticket cannot use that
+completion operation, dispatch a handler or mutate its response.
+
+## Explicit callback connection
+
+The transitive effect and replay helper surface was inventoried before adding
+connection plumbing. Fifteen service helpers carry an optional explicit
+`_connection` argument:
+
+```text
+_context, _profile, _program, _native, _build_inputs, _build_receipt,
+_subject, _verification, _check_native_refinement_evidence, _required_claims,
+_slot_snapshot, _conditional_slot, _hia_adopt, _hia_rollback,
+_replay_verification
+```
+
+Five store helpers carry it onward: `get`, `get_json`, `put`, `json` and
+`check_profile`. Calls without a supplied capability retain their original
+argument shape and official connection. There is no ambient connection
+substitution or thread-local fallback.
+
+The effect capability recognizes the twelve literal SQL statements used by
+those paths and qualifies each table as `main`. It checks creator PID, calling
+thread, exact state and connection ownership, native pending token, phase,
+mode and the still-open transaction before each operation. Its cursor wrapper
+allows guarded fetching and row-count observation, never arbitrary cursor
+execution. Replay capabilities admit only the SELECT subset. Retained
+connections and cursor views are revoked when the native phase changes.
+
+The actual adopt and rollback controls deny all SQL on the official connection
+during the handler and still complete the effect through the private
+capability. A concurrent ordinary writer blocks independently, then commits
+its own work; it cannot join or be rolled back with the private atomic effect.
+
+## Retained state and acknowledgement boundaries
+
+The main ABI uses a 128-byte request header and a 1024-byte state prefix plus a
+bounded response buffer. Runtime response capacity is 8 MiB, matching the
+existing wire bound. Tests also exercise smaller exact buffers. Request and
+connection nonces bind every transition to one state instance and connection.
+The 64-bit sequence refuses exhaustion instead of wrapping.
+
+HIA validates UTF-8 and counts Unicode scalar values for the existing eligible
+request-key length of 1 through 192 characters. A transport may carry at most
+768 key bytes. Overlong and nonstring candidates remain ineligible for a
+durable key, as in the existing service validation flow. NUL is an ordinary
+key character. The bounded row format admits canonical nonnegative decimal
+timestamps up to 64 digits and printable ASCII tool names up to 128 bytes;
+the actual service tool names and generated timestamps are within that scope.
+This does not promise equivalence for arbitrary malformed legacy SQLite rows.
+
+| Native phase | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1–5 | BEGIN, read, write, exact readback and COMMIT acknowledgement |
+| 6 | Admitted request or confirmed atomic abort, with no pending callback |
+| 7 | One callback dispatch has been claimed; its outcome is pending |
+| 8 | Completed owned response or validated durable replay |
+| 9 | Refused or uncertain state |
+| 10 | Callback rollback pending |
+| 11 | Durable replay validation pending |
+| 12 | Exact callback result captured; terminal SQL may now be requested |
+
+Phase 12 closes a reentrant completion window. A callback cannot call `finish`
+while its own result is still pending. After it returns, native state captures
+the exact serialized response before the caller receives it. Mutating the
+returned Python object cannot authorize a different terminal response.
+Interruption before or after native acknowledgement fences the request and
+preserves the original durable row for observation.
+
+### Native cleanup epochs
+
+Rollback authorization is held in native state, independently of Python error
+messages. Word 25 receives a new transaction epoch before every emitted BEGIN:
+initial reservation, atomic effect and ordinary/rejected completion. Word 19
+records the last consumed cleanup epoch.
+
+Event 91 is a separate 32-byte cleanup-claim receipt. It validates the retained
+checksum and both immutable nonces, consumes the current epoch, seals the
+state, and only then grants one rollback attempt. It does not grant dispatch,
+completion or ordinary transition authority. Repeating the claim returns no
+grant. Every explicit and exception-cleanup SQL ROLLBACK goes through this
+entry. A normal native rollback acknowledgement additionally requires the
+consumed epoch to match the current epoch.
+
+This covers a lost native return value, interruption before storing a Python
+receipt and interruption while publishing cleanup diagnostics. Those failures
+cannot restore rollback permission. A confirmed atomic abort followed by a
+separate completion transaction receives a new epoch, so legitimate later
+cleanup is still possible. If rollback cannot be confirmed, the connection
+retains its actual state owner and is fenced. Closing that connection remains
+foreign resource cleanup; it does not create a completed request or retry
+authority.
+
+`RequestJournalUnknown` is intentionally outside the service's known-error
+formatter. A lost BEGIN, COMMIT, callback outcome, native receipt or cleanup
+acknowledgement must not be turned into a completed error response. A fresh
+read of the same durable row can return an already committed exact response;
+a running row remains unknown. No alternate key or historical completion is
+invented.
+
+## Qualification and evidence
+
+The strict builder accepts only a completed source-matching cold report and
+its compiler image:
+
+```sh
+python -m tools.build_hia_request_journal \
+  --compiler /absolute/path/to/B3.image.bin \
+  --cold-report /absolute/path/to/cold-report.json \
+  --output /absolute/path/to/new-request-journal-build
+```
+
+Set `HEPTA_HIA_REQUEST_JOURNAL_MANIFEST` to the resulting `manifest.json` to
+select the runtime owner. Selection is explicit; this work does not flip a
+production default or migrate live requests.
+
+For integration tests, `HEPTA_HIA_REQUEST_JOURNAL_COLD_REPORT` selects that exact
+report and its nested final compiler image. Both request and execution-budget
+dependency images are built by their strict builders from the same report and
+compiler. Combining this with
+`HEPTA_HIA_REQUEST_JOURNAL_DEVELOPMENT_COMPILER` is an admission error. Invalid
+cold admission fails before any evidence directory or development seed is
+created. Standalone B0/B1/B2 or explicitly reused compiler runs are separately
+labelled development evidence and never relabelled as source-matched cold
+qualification.
+
+Controls include independent HIA VM versus actual machine state bytes, exact
+SQLite intent and completion, one concurrent winning owner, Unicode key
+boundaries, malformed owner tokens and retained-state corruption, real
+interpreter acknowledgement interruptions, all transaction cleanup epochs,
+readonly replay and capability revocation, TEMP namespace shadows, actual
+main/WAL/shm replacement, real ordinary-writer concurrency, actual Agent
+artifact/adopt/rollback failures, eight process-exit boundaries with restart,
+and an installed wheel with authoring and reference policy forbidden.
+
+The unchanged original Agent tool and campaign suite runs jointly with native
+request and execution-budget owners and poisoned reference constructors.
+Development runs retain 34 original cases and defer only the shared discovery
+source-contract check to integration. A matching cold fixture includes that
+original check as well, for 35 nested cases. Independent adversarial review
+also exercises exact interpreter opcode and return-value boundaries.
+
+Two actual failures are retained as failures: the original `cea9531` cleanup
+could attempt three rollbacks after one unconfirmed rollback, and `b291c7e`
+could attempt a second rollback if Python poison publication was interrupted.
+The native transaction-epoch guard in `b7be6d9` closes those reproduced cases.
+Its independent actual-machine review passed twelve scenarios without changing
+the reviewed source or image. Later fixture and test changes do not relabel the
+old failures or expand that independent review's source scope.
+
+The final author development run, `hia-request-journal-development-r8`, passed
+all 22 outer tests in 97.096 seconds with zero skips. Its nested original suite
+passed 34 cases with zero skips. The separately retained independent review
+passed twelve actual-machine scenarios. The author run uses an explicitly
+reused predecessor compiler, so these results are development evidence, not
+qualification of a new integrated cold source profile. Its exact native source

+and image hash is
+`3bf79d8e9a6353356f773bbdc8f2454e79f8952a48c96b27c6c7f45bf3e027e6`.
+
+## Remaining owners
+
+Request sequencing is now an explicit selected native owner. It does not
+replace context creation and mutation, artifact file/index policy, slot and

+## Selection and custody
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_SERVICE_EVALUATION_MANIFEST` is opt-in. A service captures an actual
+immutable HIA mapping and its held checker capability during construction.
+Ambient selector changes do not replace an existing service's mapping. A new
+service performs fresh source, manifest and executable admission. The helper is
+registered as a held service owner, not as a default Core checker selection.

+development compiler. Matching cold admission retains the original 180-second
+qualification and 3-second cleanup limits. Compilation uses the unchanged

+default, whole-stack, or source-deletion authority.

+The emitted HIA table owns branching, loops, comprehensions, generators,
+named closures and their shared cells, helper dispatch, issued effect claims,
+outcome acknowledgements and temporary/named-local retirement. Actual CPython
+3.12, 3.13 or 3.14 profile is observed by the fixed bridge; HIA chooses the
+reviewed retirement direction. Unknown future profiles are not guessed.

+The Evaluation-local literal format adds tag 6 for exactly eight IEEE binary64
+bytes. Each emitted literal index is boxed once per immutable image. Positive
+and negative zero retain distinct payloads. Existing shared compilers and
+their qualified images are unchanged.

+CALL uses fixed generated literal keyword shapes and transfers operands to the
+interpreter stack at the native claim. Keyword mapping calls have separate
+DICT_MERGE, map-retirement and CALL permissions; dictionary displays use
+DICT_UPDATE. Named closures and imports use the reviewed Build lexical and
+physical import mechanisms. Exception identity, held traceback ownership,
+PEP 479 and once-only unknown outcomes retain the shared continuation protocol.

+## Preserved evaluation order
+
+The original context's absolute `created_ns` establishes the deadline; neither
+new callbacks nor this owner renew it. Reference checks run baseline then
+candidate. Native budget claim, individual runs and terminal completion keep
+their original order. An unknown execution does not complete or refund a claim.

+evaluation receipt. Cost SQL retains `LIMIT 10001`, length/truncation observation,
+then the first 10000 rows. Numeric and buffer observations remain complete.

+wall-clock acquisition, runner subprocesses, journal or ledger providers,

+# Native slot, generation and lease ledger
+
+Status: explicitly selected development owner. The confirmed `69e97bbc` direct
+input narrowing has a native object-transport repair with independent VM and
+actual machine/domain controls. Integration and matching-source cold/full
+qualification remain separate gates. The independent reference baseline is
+Hepta `63fa2e7351c6b7e787e3834cbdbfe2307a08d872`; historical failures below remain
+unchanged evidence and are not implied passes of the revised source.
+
+The owner covers the original `main.slots`, `main.versions` and `main.leases`
+ledger: observation, exact generation/epoch CAS, first baseline retention,
+maximum-retained-generation allocation, rollback, lease acquisition, exact
+retained-row admission and release. It preserves the original database and WAL.
+
+## Boundaries
+
+The selected owner requires explicitly admitted native namespace and request
+journal dependencies before writable state is created. It cannot fall back to a
+hosted transaction when a selected native capability is unavailable. Adoption
+and rollback borrow the exact current request `_EffectConnection`; they do not
+own request reservation, response history, COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Lease acquisition
+and release use the native namespace's original-connection scope and native
+epoch. Standalone observations grant no mutation authority.
+
+HIA retains each operation's original inputs, owner and connection identity,
+scope nonce/epoch/callback token, observed rows, generation/epoch, effect sequence
+and pending outcome. A side effect requires a consumed native preclaim and a
+matching outcome. Losing a result, receipt, SQL or commit acknowledgement cannot
+restore an old action's authority. The existing request or namespace owner alone
+controls transaction cleanup.
+
+Adoption and rollback return staged results to their request owner. The exact
+response and slot writes still commit together. Direct acquire/release have no
+durable request key in the original API; this work will not invent historical
+idempotency or infer lost completion merely from current row equality.
+
+## Original behavior retained
+
+- Adoption retains generation 0 baseline on an empty slot, allocates one above
+  every retained generation, and increments epoch without u64 wrap.
+- Rollback selects an existing generation and increments epoch. It never deletes
+  versions or artifacts or reverses already performed calls.
+- A lease is an active retained row, not a one-shot execution token. Repeated and
+  concurrent invocations remain supported. Each invocation freezes the retained
+  lease identity before running the foreign child.
+- With the original built-in SQLite bindings, release marks the lease inactive
+  for future admission. It neither drains nor
+  cancels already admitted calls and does not hold the Store lock across the
+  native child. Active lease count is not actual executing-child count.
+- Stale CAS details are published only after the enclosing atomic request
+  transaction is confirmed rolled back. The snapshot remains advisory.
+
+## Explicit residual owners
+
+Context, installed profile, build/proof/evaluation evidence validation, native
+ABI admission and the actual subprocess runner remain separate existing owners.
+A native ledger does not make these foreign business/checker components, the
+Python worker protocol, CLI or Rust MCP/process runtime native. Existing namespace,
+execution-budget and request-journal owners are reused, not recreated. No default
+activation, state reset, live migration, garbage collection or old-code deletion
+is part of this development checkpoint.
+
+The full read-only baseline audit also identifies hosted context creation and
+candidate-attempt authority, cost ledger, cursors, discovery profile/manifest
+construction, tool orchestration, output schemas and worker/process reporting as
+remaining work. Their native dependencies do not imply those policies are done.
+
+## Required qualification
+
+Independent HIA VM and actual machine state observations must cover wrong
+instance/scope tokens, sequence exhaustion, stale and replayed outcomes, row and
+buffer corruption, true concurrent CAS, lost SQL/native/commit receipts and
+retained unknown owners. The old tool/campaign/byte lifecycle/lease-alias and
+request-atomicity tests remain independent references and keep their original
+limits. Selected execution must pass with old ledger bodies poisoned, include
+real child use and installed-wheel resource custody, and preserve all original
+failures as evidence. Development compiler reuse is not matching-source cold or
+whole-stack qualification.
+
+## Selection and source custody
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_SLOT_LEDGER_MANIFEST` selects the installed native image. Both
+`HEPTA_HIA_ARTIFACT_NAMESPACE_MANIFEST` and
+`HEPTA_HIA_REQUEST_JOURNAL_MANIFEST` must already have admitted their real native
+owners. Image/source admission happens before a new Store directory is created.
+An absent dependency, changed image, changed packaged HIA source or incompatible
+owner refuses selection. Selecting the ledger does not select other owners by
+implication. The hosted reference remains available only when the ledger is not
+selected; a selected failure never enters it.
+
+`tools/build_hia_slot_ledger.py` requires an actual matching-source cold report
+and compiler. It admits that report before creating the output directory, checks
+the HIA source against the full admitted source manifest, compiles it, then
+rechecks compiler, report, full source and image bytes. Its build receipt keeps
+whole-stack rewriting, default activation, arbitrary-input equivalence and old
+code deletion false. The generated HIA asset is included in the installed wheel.
+
+The test fixture honors `HEPTA_HIA_SLOT_LEDGER_COLD_REPORT` for the ledger and its
+namespace/request/budget/publication dependency builds. An explicit
+`HEPTA_HIA_SLOT_LEDGER_DEVELOPMENT_COMPILER` cannot be combined with a cold report.
+Standalone compiler reuse is labelled `DEVELOPMENT_REUSED_COMPILER`; standalone
+seed/B1/B2 construction is labelled `DEVELOPMENT_B0_B1_B2`. Evidence is retained
+under `HEPTA_HIA_SLOT_LEDGER_EVIDENCE`. Neither mode grants cold qualification.
+
+## Covered caller paths within the selected profile
+
+| Existing entry | Selected authority and ordering |
+| --- | --- |
+| `inspect_slot` / `_slot_snapshot` | Read slot, active version and count of active leases; return an advisory snapshot without a mutation capability. |
+| `_conditional_slot` | Validate generation then epoch, observe the same rows, and compare both original values in HIA. |
+| `_hia_adopt` | Preserve context/evaluation/build/proof/cost/native-ABI checks, then retain baseline if empty, fold every retained generation, insert the new version and CAS the original slot. The request owner publishes the response and commits. |
+| `_hia_rollback` | Validate retained generation before expected generation/epoch, select the retained image, verify native ABI, reobserve the original slot, then CAS to that generation with incremented epoch. The request owner commits. |
+| `acquire_slot` | Observe active generation with the original argument bindings, validate the native image, obtain OS entropy, format the UUID in HIA, execute the original INSERT, then require the native namespace's confirmed commit certificate. The output retains the original target object. |
+| `_lease` / `invoke_lease` | Admit the exact active retained row and produce a detached lease value. The unchanged invocation body freezes arguments/metadata and runs the existing child outside the ledger lock. |
+| `release_slot` | Admit the active row in the original comparison order, execute the original UPDATE using its newly retained row ID, then require the confirmed namespace epoch. No extra caller-object binding is introduced. |
+
+Seven original ledger method bodies are preserved under `_..._reference` names;
+their arguments, decorators and bodies remain the baseline reference. The
+`invoke_lease` body is unchanged. Native wrappers use retained HIA results for
+generation, epoch, slot, artifact and lease identity. They do not reproduce these
+decisions from Python booleans after an interruption.
+
+All fixed ledger SQL uses `main.`. TEMP tables cannot shadow the official
+`slots`, `versions` or `leases` tables. The conditional update binds the exact
+old name, generation, epoch, context and ABI hash, requires one affected row,
+and requires exact readback. Retained-version insertion is also read back.
+Allocation uses the maximum of all retained generation rows, so rollback cannot
+make a previously used generation available again.
+
+## Retained native state and wire protocol
+
+The flat native entry takes six machine arguments: request pointer/size, result
+pointer/capacity, retained-state pointer/capacity. The fixed prefix is 4096 bytes;
+the only variable state suffix is canonical ABI JSON, bounded by 8 MiB. The
+adapter reserves the required extent before the operation begins. A caller may
+not treat a shorter result, mismatched state copy or malformed packet as success.
+
+Each request begins with 32 little-endian u64 words (`HIASLQ01`), followed by at
+most eleven length-prefixed tagged byte fields. The header binds operation nonce,
+official connection nonce, actual connection nonce, scope kind, scope epoch,
+scope nonce, callback token, native scope-owner identity and exact sequence.
+Unused header words and fields must be canonical zero/absent. Field tags denote
+absent, UTF-8 transport, canonical artifact-reference bytes, exact integer
+transport and raw bytes. HIA admits the values after this fixed transport step.
+State version 1 covers the bounded tool/adoption/rollback protocol and its
+retained raw controls. Version 2 covers direct operations 8–11. Those requests
+carry only native-owned opaque result handles, exact boolean observations or
+sixteen entropy bytes; original input and row objects are not encoded into
+bounded byte fields.
+
+| Event | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| 0 | Initialize a fresh zeroed state with immutable operation and input-identity bindings. Original direct Python object contents retain their original mutability. |
+| 2 | Consume the exact next effect token before an effect may begin. |
+| 3 | Accept only the matching effect outcome and exact row/byte observations. |
+| 4 | Accept the matching native namespace commit certificate for direct lease mutation. |
+| 5 | Record a known validator refusal or, for direct operations, a returned foreign exception with a matching native receipt. An unconfirmed outcome cannot restore a consumed claim. |
+| 90 | Validate and copy retained native state for observation only. |
+
+Phases distinguish ready, pending effect, staged transaction result, confirmed
+completion, known refusal and unknown outcome. Sequence and generation/epoch
+exhaustion refuse instead of wrapping. A checksum covers the entire canonical
+header and captured byte extent, including direct handle identities. It does
+not hash mutable Python object contents. It detects accidental corruption; it is not a
+security boundary against malicious code in the same process recomputing it.
+
+The adapter roots `LedgerState` in `NativeSlotLedgerStore.pending` before native
+initialization or any external effect. That object retains the native buffer,
+last confirmed Python receipt, cursor, returned value, original exception and
+connection/scope binding. If native state advances but receipt assignment is
+interrupted, the old receipt cannot authorize replay: the retained pending owner
+and native sequence still prevent a new operation. Even loss of a later Python
+fence diagnostic does not clear that pending owner.
+
+## Transaction ownership and uncertain results
+
+Adoption and rollback require the exact native request `_EffectConnection`
+class, same Store, original process/thread and currently active callback token.
+The request capability permits only the fixed existing SQL aliases plus the
+identity-bound conditional slot update. A capability from another Store, a
+subclass, a revoked callback or a replay-only response cannot become writable
+by substituting the official connection. Ledger code never commits or rolls
+back a borrowed request transaction.
+
+Direct acquire/release use the same official Store connection under the shared
+Store lock and the native namespace's legacy transaction owner. After the
+transaction context returns, the ledger reads the retained native namespace
+state and requires exact owner, epoch and nonce; idle phase/action; no pending
+effect, error or forced rollback; no consumed rollback for this epoch; and a
+nonzero sequence. A false `db.in_transaction`, an equal current row or a Python

+# HIA structural resource ownership
+
+This component moves the complete policy of `qualify_vm_call_depth`,
+`analyze_static_budget`, and `qualify_bounded_resources` into the checked
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/static_budget.hiaasm` program. It also provides the
+complete whole-module resource-profile audit used at the existing private
+heap-analysis boundary. The public entry signatures and receipt schemas are
+unchanged. The default path retains the independent original implementation;
+`HEPTA_HIA_STATIC_BUDGET_MANIFEST` explicitly selects the native image. A
+selected image failure cannot delegate to the retained policy.
+
+This is a structural-resource owner, not a claim that the complete project,
+all heap analyses, normalization, JSON serialization, or verification is
+already HIA native. The controller requests the original public heap APIs at
+their original points. Those APIs are separate owners, and their current
+selection and qualification remain independent. The retained Python bodies
+are still required as review/test oracles until the complete project retires
+them through its normal qualification process.
+
+## Exact ownership
+
+HIA owns the following decisions and constructions:
+
+* Exact policy kinds and bounds, with the original order of guards for each
+  public entry. The depth entry checks its policy before verification. The
+  event entry checks allocator, tick, depth, then optional heap limits before
+  verification. The composed entry captures a shallow policy copy, checks its
+  exact inventory and values, and then verifies the input.
+* Full-module profile review, including uncalled private definitions, all
+  declaration/output types, terminators and opcodes. A bad declared type is
+  deferred until the end of its function, while an unreviewed terminator or
+  opcode refuses at its original earlier point. V8 synchronous depth permits
+  chains; V7/V8 event accounting retains the original byte-only review.
+* Closed call-graph and CFG construction, duplicate-edge elimination, stable
+  topology, first cyclic/unknown dependency refusal, and all-definition
+  coverage. The original initial lexical queue and lexical successor order
+  are preserved; newly ready nodes are appended at the queue tail.
+* Per-block and per-function allocator/tick maxima, root-inclusive call depth,
+  duplicate call-site contributions, and separate syntactic maxima for
+  allocator and tick events. A CFG loop can still receive a synchronous frame
+  certificate while failing finite event qualification.
+* Arbitrary-precision integer calculation and comparison, including numbers
+  wider than u64 and limits that have no public upper bound.
+* Optional heap-inventory completeness and value checks, per-function heap
+  comparisons before event limits, and the original function/key iteration
+  order for the first exceeded policy.
+* The complete bounded-resource composition: nested event re-verification,
+  event-row mapping, every requested V8 entry heap qualification, legacy heap
+  comparisons, shallow export-row copies, and preservation of shared counter
+  integer identities between the static receipt and export rows.
+* Every receipt/error field, all schema/profile variants, the final request
+  to serialize, and insertion of the returned digest into the chosen report.
+  No bridge-side opcode inventory, graph walk, budget comparison, row plan,
+  profile decision or error-message catalogue exists.
+
+The four original source bodies are mechanically retained as
+`_reference_audit_resource_profile`, `_reference_qualify_vm_call_depth`,
+`_reference_analyze_static_budget`, and
+`_reference_qualify_bounded_resources`. Tests compare their complete source
+segments after restoring only the original function name. This avoids an
+`ast.dump` representation dependency between Python releases. The original
+`_bound_function`, `_topological`, `_limit` and `_successors` also remain for
+independent controls and separately pending heap paths; the selected event or
+frame owner never invokes them.
+
+## Foreign continuation boundary
+
+`hepta/hia_static_budget_native.py` holds a monotonic-ID `NativeObjectPool` with explicit native-selected releases.
+Pool IDs express identity and custody, not opcodes or semantic plans. HIA
+chooses the operation, operands, order, and next phase. Fixed continuations
+perform only these operations:
+
+| Request | Fixed foreign operation |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1 | Exact built-in kind and integer sign/bit-length/low-word representation |
+| 2 | `verify_program`, followed by `as_dict`; structured-input attribute only when HIA requests it |
+| 3–5 | Shallow object copy, set construction, and requested inequality |
+| 6–7 | Dictionary-value iterator and requested item lookup |
+| 8 | Canonical sign plus little-endian integer magnitude; no decimal conversion |
+| 9 | Verified source identities, with input identity read only when requested |
+| 10–11 | Existing constant-live-heap or entry-live-heap public API |
+| 12 | Original final `json.dumps` options, UTF-8 encoding and SHA-256 |
+| 13–17 | Requested item assignment, iterator next, holding a complete HIA-produced value, sequence iterator, or release of an owned temporary handle |
+| 100–101 | Physical workspace/output growth preserving existing bytes |
+
+Python exact-object metadata is representation only. In particular, a huge
+positive integer is not decimalized merely to check its sign or compare its
+bit length. A custom key that compares equal to a required policy name is not
+prematurely rejected by a generic JSON-pool validator. Set/hash/equality/item
+operations remain explicit foreign protocols in the exact native-selected
+sequence. The final JSON operation retains its original late key-sort and
+integer-digit failures. Policy lookups use native-selected opaque references
+to the actual four Python literal objects, rather than newly decoded equal
+strings. The initial packet holds these constants as fixed representation
+data; HIA selects their IDs and decides each lookup. Temporary set results and
+iterators are released by HIA at their original completed predicate/iteration
+points. Released IDs are never reused and stale references are rejected.
+This preserves reachable custom-key identity and reference-count observations,
+without prematurely deep-copying or admitting foreign objects. The composed
+entry still performs its nested
+`analyze_static_budget` verification even when that second verification
+rejects an expanded canonical Core that passed the original first boundary.
+
+Heap continuation calls do not certify that a particular heap implementation
+is native. `analyze_constant_live_heap` and
+`qualify_entry_live_heap_budget` keep their names and signatures so the heap
+owner can independently pin or replace its own selected policy. The native
+private audit is available as
+`NativeStaticBudget.audit_resource_profile(document, schema=..., allow_chain=...)`
+for an already verified Core and the reviewed fixed schema/boolean domain.
+
+## Private framing and custody
+
+The image ABI is `(readbuf source, mutbuf output, mutbuf workspace) -> u32`.
+The executable header stores magic, phase, sequence, request and four request
+words at byte offsets 0 through 56. The shared graph arena uses offsets
+64/72/80 for used bytes, minimum requested extent and arena error. Offset 88
+is the acknowledged sequence. Status/output length/reply pointer/mode are at
+96/104/112/120. Graph writing uses 152/160 for cursor/overflow. Status 1 is a
+complete success value; status 2 is the complete semantic error pair. A
+transport invariant is refused as such and never fabricated into a budget
+receipt. Unused request words and the two optional-attribute flags must be
+canonical.
+
+Every returned frame is an exact frozen `BudgetFrame`. Its exact integer
+kinds, request words, identity, sequence, and decoder-created graph are bound
+before a foreign operation can run. Native-created dictionaries/lists retain
+shallow edge snapshots; replacement, insertion, ordering or scalar-identity
+changes are refused. Opaque referenced objects retain identity and the pool's
+stable-custody contract; their arbitrary internals are not recursively copied
+or scanned. This boundary is private transport correctness, not protection
+against hostile arbitrary code inside the same Python process.
+
+A callback permission is consumed before the callback. A completed callback
+reply is acknowledged only after materialization and storage complete. An
+exception or interrupt permanently closes the context, prevents resuming or
+replaying the request, and preserves the original foreign exception identity.
+Terminal permission is also consumed once before materializing a refusal or
+returning the already chosen object.
+
+Workspace and output growth retain both old and new mmap objects across
+assignment, interruption, and old-arena close. Partial construction and all
+abort paths release every owned arena without masking the original error.
+Revocation is permanent; physical close is retryable when an exported buffer
+causes `BufferError`. A failed close retains the object for the later retry.
+The bridge introduces no success report for a foreign `MemoryError`, JSON
+failure, Core refusal, heap refusal or callback `BaseException`. Still-live
+foreign identities remain with an exceptional context for as long as its
+original exception traceback remains held, matching the original locals'
+custody. They are not eagerly destroyed while propagating a refusal. This
+retention includes no live native arena or resumable permission. Normal
+success and explicit caller-owned private `close()` release the pool; the
+native-selected completed temporary releases still occur at their earlier
+original points.
+
+## Numeric and representation bounds
+
+There is no new public source-byte, JSON-node, output-value, counter-bit or
+limb quota. The original public normalization can admit a final Core whose
+real node inventory is larger than its earlier structural traversal saw.
+The static owner therefore uses actual representations, not a presumed
+262144-node bound.
+
+Each typed source/reply node has its own 16-byte header. The HIA reader bounds
+nodes by actual packet length divided by 16, and bounds container children by
+the actual payload extent. The decoder opts into
+`decode_bound_native_graph(..., extent_bounds=True, binary_integers=True,
+objects=...)`. Its node/concat bounds follow actual encoded extents; it does
+not import the generic codec's old fixed node/expansion quotas. The historical
+codec defaults used by other components are unchanged. Its depth 128 remains
+a private grammar bound: verified primitive Core and this fixed wrapper have
+at most ten enclosing containers, and generated receipts have fixed shallow
+shape. Arbitrary foreign objects remain opaque and are not admitted through
+that grammar.
+
+Workspace allocation follows actual packet size, actual graph inventories,
+and the proven counter width. Let `F` be the verified number of functions,
+`M` the total instruction-plus-terminator inventory, and `B=M+2`. For an
+acyclic call graph, a per-function event count is less than `B**(F+1)`:
+local events and call occurrences are bounded by `M`, and each additional
+call height multiplies the previous conservative bound by less than `B`.
+The HIA controller reserves
+`ceil(((F+1)*bit_length(B)+1)/32)` limbs for each calculated count. This is an
+allocation proof from the actual verified graph, not a cap on a supplied
+integer. Block scratch is reclaimed after each complete function; permanent
+function summaries are separate. Every base-2**32 limb occupies one u64 slot,
+so addition/multiplication intermediates satisfy the shared bigint contract.
+Static event accumulation itself only needs the shared addition/comparison
+and binary-export functions.
+
+The Core verifier's own function inventory bound remains unchanged. Counts
+can greatly exceed u64 even with only 71 functions. A policy or heap result
+may be arbitrarily wider than the calculated counter: HIA first compares
+signs and bit lengths, requesting raw magnitude bytes only when necessary.
+No supplied number is constrained to the count arena's limb capacity. The
+original final Python JSON conversion retains its own integer-digit policy
+and exact original late error channel.
+
+Output grows to the complete graph byte count requested by HIA. Large
+integers use canonical tag 12 binary magnitudes, and complete foreign values
+use explicit tag 13 pool references. Report composition does not recursively
+re-encode or duplicate opaque existing heap/event receipts. Physical address
+space or allocation exhaustion remains an ordinary foreign failure; it is
+not converted to a new language limit.
+
