+# Native task helper cache owner
+
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/task_helper_cache.hiaasm` owns the complete cache
+decision around the existing HIA task-helper generator. It performs the exact
+lookup, requests dependencies and task protocol checks in order, selects the
+poll and cancellation effect objects, admits the complete generator result,
+commits its counter and optional name, and publishes a helper only after
+successful admission. The cache belongs to the elaborator and is shared across
+functions; a controller invocation does not create a function-local cache.
+
+This is a bounded nominal compiler owner. It does not claim that every parser,
+runtime, compiler transport, release tool or other project component is HIA.
+The separately owned task generator still emits every helper instruction,
+block, effect and cleanup operation. The separately owned native type session
+still checks task protocols. This controller performs the complete surrounding
+cache policy without a selected hosted fallback.
+
+## Selection and integration
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_TASK_HELPER_CACHE_MANIFEST` selects the image. Missing, changed or
+invalid selected source, image or manifest refuses. The adapter exposes
+`selected_task_helper_cache()`, `installed_task_helper_cache(manifest)` and
+`NativeTaskHelperCache.lower(owner, typ, operation, require_native=False)`.
+
+The elaborator's selected branch precedes its old hosted cache lookup. An
+already admitted image can be supplied through the private `_native_cache`
+keyword so that a continuation never reselects a different dependency. The
+complete native function path requires this cache owner at the original task
+helper continuation. A missing cache is an explicit dependency refusal even
+if the old host dictionary happens to contain a name. Once the native cache
+is admitted, a cache hit does not select or check the helper generator.
+
+With no cache selected, ordinary callers retain the exact old wrapper in
+`_reference_helper_cache`. Its body AST hash is
+`9a2986d04df78f9c563504c9b9019808c8f728f3e22a5bfd71c300148af52947`.
+The independent test copy retains every executable statement and branch;
+only its relative import is made absolute for the test module and normalized
+back for the AST check. The original pure helper generator remains a separate
+reference control as well.
+
+## Exact order and partial state
+
+The HIA controller follows these original phases:
+
+| Phase | HIA decision and requested observation | State visible afterward |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Cache lookup | Compare the native type identity and operation with every held cache row | On a hit, return the exact held name immediately |
+| Generator selection | Request the generator selector only after a miss | Hold the returned native image for the entire continuation |
+| Task protocol | Request the already owned native type session | Preserve its exact descriptor/observation changes or refusal |
+| Effect lookup | Find poll and cancellation names in the held function inventory; request poll effects before cancellation effects | Hold the original complete effect objects |
+| Generation | Request the held HIA generator with the current serial and complete descriptors/effects | Hold its complete result without admitting or publishing it |
+| Prefix commit | Copy the generator's serial and cache its name when non-null | A failed generation can already have a cached name |
+| Admission | Propagate the generator's exact error code/message | A refusal keeps the serial and name prefix |
+| Publication | Append the complete held helper and return its held name | Successful name/helper objects preserve their identity |
+
+The five operations are `start`, `poll`, `cancel`, `join` and `close`. The
+generator owns fresh-name allocation. For example, when generation starts at
+serial 8191, it can reserve `h2internal_8192` and then refuse further expansion;
+that name remains cached without a helper. Starting at 8192 produces no new
+name. A later hit returns an already cached name without another check,
+generation, counter update or append, including when generator selection has
+since become unavailable.
+
+The old wrapper reads both effect objects before invoking the native
+generator. The controller keeps that order for every operation. It does not
+pre-read the effects of unrelated functions. A missing held function key is
+reported through a dedicated native-chosen `KeyError` continuation; this
+preserves direct private-call behavior when a function map has been altered
+after protocol checking. Public task protocol admission remains a separate
+owner and retains its existing errors.
+
+On a generator miss with no generator selected, `require_native=True` retains
+`E_HIA_TYPE: selected native function requires native task helper generation`.
+An explicitly selected cache with `require_native=False` also refuses rather
+than using a hosted generator, with the cache-specific dependency message.
+The flag is a private controller option, not a source-language field.
+
+## Issued graph integrity
+
+The recovery audit retained three actual-image negative observations. On the
+original cache bridge, changing a terminal empty serial array to contain 99
+caused an unissued owner write. Changing the issued generator serial from 0
+to 77 reached the actual helper image and generated `h2internal_78`. The
+function bridge separately allowed an issued parameter path to be changed.
+These are private transport correctness findings, not a claim about defending
+against arbitrary code running in the same process. The original observations
+and sources remain in the separately retained original-failure archive.
+
+The corrected bridge uses `decode_bound_native_graph`. While decoding, it
+captures immutable shallow edges for every newly created list and dictionary,
+including decoded source references. It validates those edges before consuming
+a callback or commit permission and before any owner write. Changed keys,
+typed scalar identities, nested edges, inserted cycles and copied replacement
+objects refuse. Terminal admission requires the exact issued result and its
+unchanged header as well as the unchanged graph. A refusal closes the context
+and releases the binding and both arenas without applying a new prefix.
+
+Concatenations retain their source pieces and lengths rather than allocating
+another expanded array. New scalar/string bytes are not copied. Binding space
+follows wire-created edges and encoded piece references, not repeated logical
+aliases. Existing node, depth, byte, expansion and public language limits are
+unchanged.
+
+Tags 10 and 11 preserve the exact identities of previously held external
+helpers/Core objects. Their interiors are opaque and retain the existing
+stable-pool custody contract. In particular, simultaneously changing a held
+external list and the new concatenated outer list is outside this binding's
+guarantee. The binding does not deep-copy or traverse opaque interiors to
+invent an immutable history of another owner's objects. An outer list newly
+materialized from an external tuple is bound; its children remain opaque.
+
+## Transport and ownership
+
+The bridge accepts only `_NativeTypeIdentity` keys already issued by HIA.
+Each identity includes a session nonce and unsigned identifier. It transports
+the identifier after checking that all held keys have the query's exact nonce;
+it never projects, hashes, compares or reconstructs hosted structural type
+keys. Repeated equal nominal descriptors are already interned by the native
+type owner. A cache hit needs the held key, not a live type arena. A miss
+requires the native type session for the requested task protocol check.
+
+The input is a typed value packet:
+
+```text
+[metadata, sequence, current_serial, reply, function_inventory]
+metadata = [type_id, operation, require_native, cache_rows, invocation_nonce]
+cache_row = [type_id, operation, name, external_name_id]
+function_inventory = [poll_name, cancel_name, function_names]
+generator_reply = [serial, error, name, external_name_id, external_helper_id]
+```
+
+Metadata is captured byte for byte in the native workspace. Every continuation
+must repeat it exactly. The function inventory is observed only when requested,
+then similarly retained and compared by complete bytes. Invocation nonces
+prevent swapping equal-looking metadata between independently owned contexts.
+No user-supplied manifest or source field controls packet regions or limits.
+
+Cache values and the generator's complete name/helper use the existing generic
+`NativeValuePool`. HIA writes external references into a complete result graph;
+the bridge does not rebuild Core or interpret a language-specific lowering
+plan. The final result contains complete `serial`, `cache`, `helpers` update
+arrays and the returned `name`. Each update array has zero or one element.
+Materialization applies the first two arrays, performs admission, then appends
+the helper array. There is no hosted branch deciding whether a key hit, which
+name to generate, whether to cache a failed name or when to publish a helper.
+
+The output header contains eight unsigned 64-bit words: magic, error, request,
+payload size, sequence, and three reserved zeros. Requests are:
+
+| Request | Fixed transport operation |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1 | Select and retain the native helper generator |
+| 2 | Invoke the retained native task protocol owner |
+| 3 | Hold the current complete function inventory |
+| 4 | Fetch effects at the HIA-selected function ordinal and argument slot |
+| 5 | Invoke the retained generator at the HIA-selected serial |
+| 6 | Raise the missing key selected by HIA |
+| 0 | Materialize the complete terminal result |
+
+The bridge accepts only the exact current request/query pair. It consumes a
+request permission before any external callback, accepts a new native step
+only after the prior callback completes, and closes on interruption. Every
+public `lower` invocation releases both arenas in `finally`. Partial
+constructor allocations are released inside the constructor itself, before
+that public `finally` has received a context. Retaining the original exception
+and traceback must not retain an abandoned arena or make the callback
+re-serviceable. Original owner/type/cache prefixes remain visible.
+
+## Private capacity proof
+
+Public limits are unchanged: 8 MiB source, 262,144 JSON nodes, depth 64, 1,024
+functions, 128 nominal instances, 512 flat slots per type, 32,768 charged value
+slots and serial at most 8192. This controller does not charge new public
+slots, flatten values or change expansion limits.
+
+At most 128 task instances can occupy the nominal-instance inventory. Each
+has five helper keys, so 640 cache rows is conservative. At most 1,024 function
+names are observed. Public names have at most 128 ASCII bytes; generated names
+are shorter, but the private calculation allows 128 bytes for every cached
+name too. The private limits are:
+
+| Region | Capacity |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Input packet | 1,048,576 bytes |
+| Typed decoded values | 8,192 nodes |
+| Typed nesting | 128 |
+| Output frame | 4,096 bytes |
+| Workspace | 2,097,152 bytes |
+| Captured metadata | 262,144 bytes |
+| Captured function inventory | 262,144 bytes |
+
+A cache row has five typed nodes including its array, and at most 235 bytes
+using a ten-digit identifier, six-byte operation, 128-byte name and three-digit
+pool index. All 640 rows therefore use at most 150,400 bytes and 3,200 nodes.
+The row array and surrounding metadata contribute fewer than 512 further
+bytes and 16 nodes. The function inventory uses at most 147,792 bytes and
+1,028 nodes. The root, serial, sequence and largest generator reply keep the
+whole packet below 310,000 bytes and 4,300 nodes. Its actual nesting is shallow;
+the 128-level transport guard is conservative. The independent envelope test
+uses 640 rows and 1,024 long names without asserting that those artificial
+private IDs are newly admitted public task definitions.
+
+Workspace regions are disjoint. Parser scratch ends below offset 4096; the
+output writer uses offset 4096; controller state begins at 8192. The duplicate
+key table occupies `[16384, 26624)`. Metadata occupies at most
+`[32768, 294912)`, and the function inventory at most `[327680, 589824)`.
+These remain below the two-MiB arena. Every region copy checks its extent.
+
+The complete terminal graph needs fewer than 1,024 output bytes even with all
+three updates present. The large helper is an external reference, not a

+# Native ordinary task instruction lowering
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_TASK_OPERATIONS_MANIFEST` explicitly selects the complete HIA owner
+of the ordinary `task.create`, `task.state`, `task.start`, `task.poll`,
+`task.cancel`, `task.join` and `task.close` branches. HIA owns their semantic
+guards, type comparisons, linear transfer, fresh names, complete value
+bindings and emitted primitive Core instructions. It also owns rejection of
+an unknown ordinary task operation, after the original attribute/argument
+guards. An operator-owned manifest binds the checked
+`examples/hia_bootstrap/task_operations.hiaasm`, image and compiler digests.
+Source programs cannot choose this manifest. A selected image/source,
+transport, continuation or semantic failure never executes the retained task
+reference branch.
+
+The surrounding function/SSA traversal, ordinary call/primitive branches,
+terminators and final primitive verification retain their existing owners.
+Type and protocol resolution and task-helper generation are separate existing
+owners, each with its own explicit native selection. This implementation does
+not claim completion of the whole elaborator or the whole system. Accepted
+source versions and normalized targets remain composite v1 to Core v6,
+composite v2/v3 to Core v7, and composite v4 to Core v8.
+
+## Complete responsibilities
+
+| Operation | Native responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| `task.create` | Empty attributes, declared task/input arity, protocol-check request at its original point, state-type equality, state consumption, zero tag/token/result padding, every fresh name and the complete task binding. |
+| `task.state` | Task input guard, both primitive-resolution requests around output reparse/comparison, exact last-resolved primitive identity, and alias to the original tag. |
+| `task.start`, `task.poll`, `task.cancel` | Task input and output checks, consumption, complete fresh output binding, helper request after that prefix, and the complete primitive call after helper success. |
+| `task.join` | Result type/arity, consumption, fresh result names including a zero-width nominal result, helper continuation and complete call. |
+| `task.close` | Empty output inventory, consumption, helper continuation and complete call with no results. |
+
+The bridge copies complete native instructions and bindings; it does not
+generate names, select the expected result type, decide consumption, compute
+task layout offsets, invent padding or interpret a lowering plan. New bindings
+retain the exact descriptor selected by HIA and begin with `external=false`
+and `consumed=false`. The source branch body is retained unchanged as an
+independent reference.
+
+## Continuations and observable ordering
+
+The enclosing function resolves each argument and the initially declared
+outputs before entering an instruction branch. Later owner calls happen only
+in response to a native query, preserving their original position.
+
+| Branch | Native phases and requests |
+| --- | --- |
+| Create | Phase 0 requests `check_task(task_type)`; phase 1 compares the state and performs the complete construction. |
+| State | Phase 0 requests `resolve("u8")`; phase 1 requests output reparse; phase 2 compares outputs and requests the final `resolve("u8")`; phase 3 binds that exact final descriptor. |
+| Start/poll/cancel/join/close | Phase 0 requests output reparse; phase 1 compares outputs, consumes input, allocates names and binds the complete result before requesting the helper; phase 2 emits the complete call using the returned helper name and updated counter. |
+
+Requests 1, 2 and 3 carry no instructions, new bindings, changed flags or fresh
+counter. Request 4 is intentionally different: it carries the already
+completed consumption/output-binding prefix. The bridge applies that prefix
+before invoking the existing `helper(task_type, operation)` owner. Only HIA
+selects the type and operation in this request.
+
+The original expression evaluates helper generation before appending its
+primitive call. Consequently a helper failure must preserve the consumed
+input, completed output binding and fresh counter, but must not append a call.
+The helper may also have allocated and cached its own name before failing to
+complete its function. Those changes remain in the helper owner exactly as
+before. A subsequent lookup can reuse that cached name; the native ordinary
+branch preserves this direct-owner partial-state behavior. Final program
+verification continues to check that every emitted call has a valid callee.
+
+After helper success, the bridge transports its returned name, current serial
+and the exact native-issued prefix bindings back to HIA. The final native
+entry verifies that prefix's descriptor, output name, ordered generated names,
+consumption and counter bounds before constructing the call. It emits no
+duplicate binding and allocates no additional name. The bridge neither
+reconstructs a call nor replays the consumed operation in Python.
+
+Create has similarly exact failure prefixes: its state is consumed before the
+tag, token and result padding are built. A fresh-name failure between the
+constant, buffer owner and success flag preserves the operations and counter
+already produced. The task binding is installed only after every padding slot
+succeeds. State projection never consumes its task, and a refusal during any
+of its three primitive resolutions leaves the output unbound.
+
+## Private packet and admission
+
+```text
+[phase, serial, operation, attributes, descriptors, values, arguments,
+ initial_declared_outputs, owner_receipts, reparsed_outputs_or_null,
+ helper_name_or_null, prefix_or_null]
+descriptor = [kind, primitive_flat_types, linear, state_type_id_or_null, result_type_id_or_null]
+value = [type_id, primitive_names, external, consumed]
+argument = [source_name, value_id]
+declared_output = [source_name, type_id]
+prefix = [serial_after_output_allocation, native_bindings]
+binding = [source_name, type_id, primitive_names, false, false]
+```
+
+Every held value is transported once, with each argument occurrence retaining
+its value ID. Existing type sessions intern repeated nominal descriptors;
+their identities are preserved without hashing/comparing semantic keys or
+expanding a type graph. HIA compares nominal IDs and primitive names. Only task
+state/result references are needed for these branches; record field graphs and
+enum payload graphs remain the responsibility of their existing type owners.
+
+Admission checks exact inventories, index bounds, booleans, source/generated
+names, primitive layouts, task tag/token/state/result concatenation, cumulative
+value slots and phase-specific receipts. It verifies the saved prefix before
+using any of its names. This is a representation of held, admitted types, not
+a new source declaration interface or user-controlled compilation manifest.
+
+The image has private 256-MiB input, 8-MiB output and 16-MiB scratch regions.
+The typed arena validator independently checks bytes, 8,388,608 nodes and depth
+128. Public limits remain 8-MiB source, 262,144 JSON value nodes, depth 64,
+128 nominal instantiations, 512 primitive layout slots, 32,768 elaborated value
+slots and 8,192 generated names.
+
+Let `N = 262144`, `V = 32768` and
+`D <= 2*V + 2*128 + 128 + 2 = 65922`. Held values and initially declared outputs
+share the first value-slot quota; output reparse can add another `V` primitive
+descriptor objects. Each cached task contributes at most two additional
+primitive state/result descriptors. There are at most 128 cached nominal
+descriptors and two state-projection resolution receipts. Zero-width values
+and repeated arguments do not create distinct nominal descriptors.
+
+| Packet component | Conservative typed-node bound |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Attributes including object keys | `2*N` |
+| Held values and physical names | `5*N + V` |
+| Argument occurrences | `3*N` |
+| Initial and reparsed output rows | `6*N` |
+| Descriptors and flat layouts | `7*D + 128*512` |
+| Saved output names, receipts and inventory containers | `544` |
+| Total | `4,754,606` |
+
+Charging 24 bytes to every typed node, four further public 8-MiB payload
+allowances, all held physical names and all descriptor/primitive strings keeps
+the packet below 192 MiB. Task links are indices, so nested task declarations
+cannot expand transport depth. Attributes lose their original source
+ancestors, and the private envelopes are shallow. These bounds therefore
+preserve accepted source profiles and original semantic errors for rejected
+wide instructions, rather than narrowing source arity to fit a private packet.
+
+Fixed scratch tables/state occupy 6,303,744 bytes. The largest create has an
+empty state and 510 buffer result slots: tag plus token plus result padding use
+at most 1,534 fresh names, 1,023 primitive operations and 98,248 dynamic scratch
+bytes, below a further 128 KiB. A helper-prefix entry needs at most 512 fresh
+output names; its final call entry uses no fresh names and less than 16 KiB of
+dynamic scratch. Consumption flags for `N` values plus all operations,
+bindings and queries fit below 3 MiB of output. Every entry uses private
+buffers, resets its used tables and verifies that input bytes were unchanged.
+
+The header is eight little-endian u64 words: magic `HIATOP01`, semantic error,
+final serial, request, payload length and three reserved zeros. The normal
+return extent is 64 plus the payload length; ABI refusal returns `0xfffffff1`.
+Payload keys are exactly `ops`, `consumed`, `values` and `query`. The adapter
+checks strict JSON, complete inventories, counters, continuation order and
+query framing before applying any returned state. Image custody is not a
+sandbox for arbitrary machine code or an all-input equivalence proof.
+
+## Evidence and qualification scope
+
+The native tests compare exact normalized Core for all four source versions,
+runtime results/resource cleanup, original errors and counter boundaries.
+Direct differential runs use the unchanged original branch and its actual
+enclosing closures, restoring env/ops/type caches/helper caches separately.
+They compare complete operation prefixes, bindings, flags, counters, helper
+functions, cached names and method-call ordering, including failures and a
+cached-name retry. The last resolved `u8` descriptor is checked by object
+identity, and each of its three possible callback failures is exercised.
+
+Independent HIA VM/native bytes cover every continuation kind and partial
+construction failure. Separate controls cover a 512-slot task, zero-width
+state/result, inactive loan refusal, repeated zero-width arguments, the exact
+global value-slot boundary, malformed continuation prefixes, short regions,
+depth and concurrent entries. Seven selected native nominal owners compose
+with all seven corresponding hosted references disabled. Actual machine
+allocation/free failure controls and retained task trap/rejection cases check
+execution meaning. Installed-wheel tests run without authoring tools or either
+task reference owner, and reject missing/changed packaged source and malformed
+manifests.
+
+`HEPTA_HIA_TASK_OPERATIONS_COLD_REPORT` requests the matching-source cold build
+fixture. `HEPTA_HIA_TASK_OPERATIONS_DEVELOPMENT_MANIFEST` is explicitly
+development-only; setting both is rejected. Default bootstrapped fixtures are
+labelled `BOOTSTRAP_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY`. A pinned predecessor compiler remains
+development evidence for this new source, even if its bytes were previously
+cold-qualified. Whole-profile registration, fresh cold qualification and any
+retirement decision are separate gates.

+# Unified candidate source and retained evidence binding
+
+## Concrete defect
+
+At main 5831f52fada45e076f8f68f198a15c0585e6104f, the worker's installation
+manifest includes all declared NATIVE_SOURCE_FILES and PUBLICATION_BUILD_FILES.
+That is 34 native language sources and four publication build inputs. The
+independent candidate preflight counted Python and discovery documents only.
+Its independently computed worker digest therefore could not match the actual
+current worker. A clean checkout was insufficient to prepare a joint candidate.
+
+The preflight now reads those literal source inventories without importing or
+evaluating the selected contract, snapshots every declared asset, and checks
+each actual Git blob against the selected revision. Redefined, computed,
+duplicate, escaping and symlinked inventories refuse. Historical workers with
+neither optional inventory retain their previous empty native asset domain.
+
+A new current-source regression invokes the actual worker's read-only
+installation-manifest command and compares its digest with the independent
+inventory. The original 34 preflight tests remain selected in the separate
+candidate identity workflow. The new 17 tests cover the actual manifest
+comparison and explicit synthetic identity/evidence refusal boundaries.
+Synthetic records are never native execution evidence.
+
+## Explicit native helper selection
+
+The optional worker configuration pair is:
+
+- native_helpers_manifest: the already authorized absolute path to the selected
+  helper bundle.
+- native_helpers_sha256: the SHA-256 of the bundle's exact original bytes.
+
+Both must be present or absent. The manifest path remains subject to the
+existing host read and protected-path rules. No host, command, path grant or
+write authority is added. The configured pair is passed to the worker's
+read-only installation-manifest command, whose actual fourth installation pin
+must match. Existing three-pin configurations retain their wire domain.
+
+Preparation runs where the selected source and native helper inputs can
+actually be read. A remote path is not translated into a local file or fetched
+under another identity. The worker loader remains responsible for validating
+each selected helper manifest, actual native image, source identity and ABI.
+Preflight rereads the selected bundle's digest before returning and when
+reloading the candidate; it does not activate an additional mapping.
+
+## Native support identity
+
+New candidates retain native_support_identity, containing the exact support
+contract digest, profile, target, ABI, support-domain digest, syntax digest,
+limits digest and complete source-manifest digest.
+
+These fields identify the declared bounded Selfhost-Core domain. They do not
+make direct, Selfhost, standalone and ordinary Core support identical. The
+complete existing support document remains the authority for limitations such
+as internal multi-return bounds, tail recursion, resource ownership, libc
+allocation obligations and public ABI restrictions.
+
+The original source_qualified field still means exact source/configuration
+identity. It does not mean native execution, whole-candidate acceptance or
+deployment.
+
+## Original evidence bundle
+
+Preparation accepts optional --qualification-evidence and
+--qualification-evidence-sha256 arguments, supplied together. The input file
+has this exact shape:
+
+    {
+      "schema": "hepta.hia.unified-candidate-evidence.v1",
+      "artifacts": {
+        "cold": {"path": "/absolute/original-cold.json", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>"},
+        "language": {"path": "/absolute/original-language.json", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>"},
+        "language_assertions": {"path": "/absolute/original-language.assertions.json", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>"},
+        "native_image": {"path": "/absolute/hia-native", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>"},
+        "native_build": {"path": "/absolute/build.json", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>"}
+      }
+    }
+
+The inventory can be partial. Every supplied entry must have exact bytes,
+a supported schema and compatible source identity; unknown artifact types
+refuse. Missing entries stay missing. All source files declared by the support
+contract are reread and checked against the selected Git commit, including
+files hidden from ordinary Git status with assume-unchanged.
+
+The retained component gates are:
+
+| Gate | Required binding |
+| --- | --- |
+| cold | Original outer cold report, exact source/profile, all eleven original checks, zero integer exit, unchanged 180-second qualification and 3-second cleanup limits, observed original owner completion/cleanup, and identical three-generation compiler digests. |
+| language | Original language report on the same source/profile, complete reported check counts, both compiler modes, the six fixed source/reference/fixed-point checks, exact original ten-test native assertion report, and the same compiler as the cold report. |
+| native_image_build | Original agent-stdio build receipt, the three declared dispatch/packer/frontend sources, the exact successful cold report and compiler, actual canonical Linux x86-64 ELF headers/segments and exact executable digest/length. |
+| native_worker | Not established by these build reports. Durable ordinary MCP request, replay, unknown-outcome, restart, rollback and lease consumption need their own actual worker qualification. |
+
+A failed original cold report remains failed. A timeout is not repaired by a
+later unrelated successful report, and a missing language/native job is not
+converted into success. All supplied artifact digests remain in the candidate
+for original-result custody. Reloading checks these exact bytes again.
+
+The bundle checks local artifact integrity and consistency of retained finite
+component reports. It is not an independent execution attestation, a signature
+authority or a proof of all admitted programs. The build record alone does not
+prove that MCP used the native image.
+
+## Qualification result and compatibility
+
+Every newly prepared candidate includes qualification.status = HOLD and
+whole_candidate_qualified = false until the separate native-worker requirement
+is established. Even three passing retained component gates leave this
+boundary explicit. Source pinning, supplied capture verification and actual
+catalog discovery cannot silently acquire whole-candidate qualification.
+
+The existing unified-candidate.v1 wire format remains additive. Legacy
+candidates without the new evidence fields keep their original reading
+behavior; all existing source, transport, tool and configuration pins still
+apply. The preflight never rewrites an old candidate or treats a changed
+preflight implementation as the originally pinned tool.
+
+The separate GitHub workflow preserves the checked-out commit/tree, relevant
+source/test digests and the full original unittest log on both success and
+failure. Its result covers candidate identity boundaries only. Existing Core,
+cold, language and native workflows remain required and unchanged by this
+workflow.
